This document 1) loads region-class assignments made from a trained
StarSpace model (nearest-label cosine clustering, computed in
`src/7_Evaluating_reninness_scoring_tool.ipynb`), 2) compares them to DESeq2
differentially-accessible region sets, and 3) plots tornado signal
profiles of motif-bound regions stratified by both axes.

# 8b. Load StarSpace region clusters

Region-to-label assignment is done in
`src/7_Evaluating_reninness_scoring_tool.ipynb` ("Region embedding colored by
nearest-label cluster"), which writes `bed/cluster_regions.csv`. That notebook
already reads `model.tsv` to draw the region embedding, so clustering there
keeps one implementation instead of two that can drift; it also puts the
cluster figure and the log2FoldChange figure on the same fitted embedding.

Each region is assigned to the label vector it is closest to by cosine
similarity, giving one cluster per trained label — `Renin` / `Non_Renin` for a
2-label model, `Control` / `Tumoral` / `Renin` for a 3-label one. Re-run that
notebook section to refresh the CSV after training a new model.

```{r}
cluster_csv <- file.path(bed_dir, "cluster_regions.csv")
if (!file.exists(cluster_csv)) {
  stop(cluster_csv, " not found. Run the 'Region embedding colored by ",
       "nearest-label cluster' section of ",
       "src/7_Evaluating_reninness_scoring_tool.ipynb, which writes it.")
}
starspace_regions <- read.csv(cluster_csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

stopifnot(all(c("title", "id", "start", "end") %in% names(starspace_regions)))
message(sprintf("Loaded %s regions from %s | clusters: %s",
                format(nrow(starspace_regions), big.mark = ","), cluster_csv,
                paste(sprintf("%s=%s", names(table(starspace_regions$title)),
                              format(as.numeric(table(starspace_regions$title)),
                                     big.mark = ",")),
                      collapse = ", ")))
```


# 8c. Process DESeq2 differential regions

## Load DESeq2 reports

```{r}
primary_normal <- readGeneric(primary_normal_file, chr = 1, start = 2, end = 3,
                              keep.all.metadata = TRUE, zero.based = FALSE,
                              remove.unusual = FALSE, header = TRUE,
                              skip = 0, sep = ",")
primary_high <- readGeneric(primary_high_file, chr = 1, start = 2, end = 3,
                            keep.all.metadata = TRUE, zero.based = FALSE,
                            remove.unusual = FALSE, header = TRUE,
                            skip = 0, sep = ",")
as_normal <- readGeneric(as_normal_file, chr = 1, start = 2, end = 3,
                         keep.all.metadata = TRUE, zero.based = FALSE,
                         remove.unusual = FALSE, header = TRUE,
                         skip = 0, sep = ",")
absFoldChange = 2
fdr = 0.01
```

## Load universe

```{r}
universe <- read.table(universe_file, sep = "\t", header = FALSE,
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
universe_keys <- paste(universe[, 1], universe[, 2], universe[, 3], sep = "_")
length(universe_keys)
```

## Filter into up / down sets

```{r}
primary_normal <- subset(primary_normal, pvalue < fdr)
primary_normal_up <- subset(primary_normal, log2FoldChange >=  absFoldChange)
primary_normal_down <- subset(primary_normal, log2FoldChange <= -absFoldChange)

primary_high <- subset(primary_high, pvalue < fdr)
primary_high_up <- subset(primary_high, log2FoldChange >=  absFoldChange)
primary_high_down <- subset(primary_high, log2FoldChange <= -absFoldChange)

as_normal <- subset(as_normal, pvalue < fdr)
as_normal_up <- subset(as_normal, log2FoldChange >=  absFoldChange)
as_normal_down <- subset(as_normal, log2FoldChange <= -absFoldChange)
```

## Build cross-contrast intersection sets

```{r}
lst_up <- list(
  paste(as.data.frame(as_normal_up)$seqnames,        as.data.frame(as_normal_up)$start,        as.data.frame(as_normal_up)$end,        sep = "_"),
  paste(as.data.frame(primary_normal_up)$seqnames,   as.data.frame(primary_normal_up)$start,   as.data.frame(primary_normal_up)$end,   sep = "_"),
  paste(as.data.frame(primary_high_up)$seqnames,     as.data.frame(primary_high_up)$start,     as.data.frame(primary_high_up)$end,     sep = "_")
)

lst_down <- list(
  paste(as.data.frame(as_normal_down)$seqnames,      as.data.frame(as_normal_down)$start,      as.data.frame(as_normal_down)$end,      sep = "_"),
  paste(as.data.frame(primary_normal_down)$seqnames, as.data.frame(primary_normal_down)$start, as.data.frame(primary_normal_down)$end, sep = "_"),
  paste(as.data.frame(primary_high_down)$seqnames,   as.data.frame(primary_high_down)$start,   as.data.frame(primary_high_down)$end,   sep = "_")
)

# Count DISTINCT contrasts per region, matching venn()/fromList() in
# 3_plot_genomic_distributions.Rmd: a key duplicated inside one contrast must
# not reach 2 on its own.
counts_up   <- table(unlist(lapply(lst_up,   unique)))
counts_down <- table(unlist(lapply(lst_down, unique)))

inc <- names(counts_up)  [counts_up   >= 2]
dec <- names(counts_down)[counts_down >= 2]

```

# 8d. Overlap analysis between DESeq2 and StarSpace

## Build region categories

One region-key set per trained StarSpace label + DESeq2 calls (`inc`,
`dec`, `nd`). `nd` is just `universe - inc - dec`, drawn from the BED
loaded in 8c.

`r` is the focal cluster (`focus_label`) and `nr` pools every other
label, which is what keeps the rest of the document a two-sided
renin-vs-rest comparison however many labels the model was trained with.
The ambiguous `other` band that `margin_threshold` can produce is a
non-answer, not a cluster, so it is excluded from `nr` rather than
pooled into it.

```{r}
ss_key  <- paste(starspace_regions$id, starspace_regions$start,
                 starspace_regions$end, sep = "_")
ss_sets <- split(ss_key, factor(starspace_regions$title,
                                levels = unique(starspace_regions$title)))

ambiguous_label <- "other"   # the notebook's margin band, if it was used
cluster_labels  <- setdiff(names(ss_sets), ambiguous_label)
stopifnot(focus_label %in% cluster_labels)
# Focus first, so set order in the UpSet plot and in `sets` below is stable
# across models rather than following model.tsv's vocabulary order.
cluster_labels  <- c(focus_label, setdiff(cluster_labels, focus_label))

r  <- ss_sets[[focus_label]]
nr <- unlist(ss_sets[setdiff(cluster_labels, focus_label)], use.names = FALSE)

nd <- setdiff(c(r, nr), c(inc, dec))

message(sprintf("StarSpace clusters: %s | pooled non-%s = %s",
                paste(sprintf("%s=%s", names(ss_sets),
                              format(lengths(ss_sets), big.mark = ",")),
                      collapse = ", "),
                focus_label, format(length(nr), big.mark = ",")))
```

## UpSet plot

```{r}
# UpSetR's fromList() runs the names through data.frame(), which would
# mangle "Non-renin" into "Non.renin" and break the `sets =` lookup below.
# Slugging to "Non_renin" here reproduces the historical 2-label naming.
disp        <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", cluster_labels)
focus_disp  <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", focus_label)
deseq_sets  <- list(Increase = inc, Decrease = dec, Non_differential = nd)

listInput_all <- c(deseq_sets, setNames(ss_sets[cluster_labels], disp))

svg(file.path(plot_dir, "ss_deseq_upset.svg"), width = 10, height = 6, onefile = FALSE)
upset(fromList(listInput_all),
      mainbar.y.label = "overlapped regions",
      sets.x.label = "regions per group",
      sets = c(names(deseq_sets), disp),
      keep.order = TRUE, order.by = "freq",
      show.numbers = "yes",
      set_size.show = TRUE,
      set_size.scale_max = max(lengths(listInput_all)) * 1.2,
      text.scale = c(1.5,1.5,1.5,1.5,1.75,1.5))
dev.off()

# Every DESeq2 call x every StarSpace label. With 3+ labels the pooled
# "non-<focus>" complement is appended as well, since it is the set the
# tornado / GO steps downstream actually consume; with 2 labels the single
# other label already IS that complement, so it is not duplicated.
sets <- list()
for (d in names(deseq_sets)) {
  for (i in seq_along(cluster_labels)) {
    sets[[paste0(d, ":", disp[i])]] <-
      intersect(deseq_sets[[d]], ss_sets[[cluster_labels[i]]])
  }
  if (length(cluster_labels) > 2) {
    sets[[paste0(d, ":non_", focus_disp)]] <- intersect(deseq_sets[[d]], nr)
  }
}
lengths(sets)
```

# 8e. Write intersection BED files

```{r}
write_set_bed <- function(peaks, out_path) {
  df <- data.frame(peaks = peaks)
  df <- df %>%
    extract(peaks, c("seqname", "start", "end"), regex = "(.*)_([^_]+)_([^_]+)$")
  df <- df[order(df$seqname, df$start), ]
  write.table(df, out_path, row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE,
              sep = "\t", col.names = FALSE)
  GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(df)
}

# Filename convention, unchanged for 2-label models: the focal cluster is
# "_r" and the pooled complement is "_nr", giving exactly the historical six
# (inc_r, inc_nr, dec_r, dec_nr, nd_r, nd_nr) that 8g reloads and 8j reuses.
# With 3+ labels each individual non-focal label additionally gets its own
# file (inc_control.bed, inc_tumoral.bed, ...) next to the pooled "_nr" one.
bed_prefix <- c(Increase = "inc", Decrease = "dec", Non_differential = "nd")
bed_suffix <- function(label_part) {
  if (label_part == focus_disp)                            "r"
  else if (label_part == paste0("non_", focus_disp))       "nr"
  else if (length(cluster_labels) == 2)                    "nr"
  else                                        tolower(label_part)
}

gr_sets <- list()
for (nm in names(sets)) {
  parts <- strsplit(nm, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  var   <- paste(bed_prefix[[parts[1]]], bed_suffix(parts[2]), sep = "_")
  gr_sets[[var]] <- write_set_bed(sets[[nm]],
                                  file.path(bed_dir, paste0(var, ".bed")))
  message(sprintf("  %-16s -> %-14s %s regions", nm, paste0(var, ".bed"),
                  format(length(sets[[nm]]), big.mark = ",")))
}

# Named variables the rest of the document (8g-8j) refers to directly.
#
# Every set written above is bound to a variable, not just the pooled six.
# With a 3-label model that is the full 3 x 3 grid -- inc_r/inc_control/
# inc_tumoral, dec_*, nd_* -- plus the pooled inc_nr/dec_nr/nd_nr that 8j
# still consumes. 8g-8i treat Control and Tumoral as SEPARATE feature sets,
# so binding only the pooled names here (as this chunk used to) left the
# in-memory path out of sync with the reload path in 8g.
#
# Short aliases mirror the reload block in 8g: _c = Control, _t = Tumoral.
for (v in names(gr_sets)) assign(v, gr_sets[[v]])

alias <- c(control = "c", tumoral = "t")
for (cat in c("inc", "dec", "nd")) {
  for (long in names(alias)) {
    from <- paste(cat, long, sep = "_")
    if (!is.null(gr_sets[[from]]))
      assign(paste(cat, alias[[long]], sep = "_"), gr_sets[[from]])
  }
}

message("Bound ", length(gr_sets), " set variables: ",
        paste(sort(names(gr_sets)), collapse = ", "))
```

# 8f. StarSpace embedding vs DESeq2 differential accessibility

Two diagnostics tying the trained StarSpace embedding back to the DESeq2
calls. This section runs before the tornado plots (8g–8i) so the
embedding ↔ DE relationship is validated first, and the cos-sim values
are available to inform tornado feature-set selection downstream.

1.  **Scatter** — cosine similarity of each region embedding to the
    trained `Renin` label embedding vs DESeq2 log2 fold change, faceted
    by contrast. If the StarSpace model learned "renin-like
    accessibility," cos-sim should track log2FC; per-facet Spearman ρ
    quantifies that.
2.  **Binned line plot** — % of regions called differential by DESeq2 as
    a function of cos-sim, in quantile bins. This is the figure that
    shows how the DESeq2 call rate rises with embedding proximity.
    Pooled-across-contrasts and per-contrast views are both produced.
    It is read, not thresholded: nothing downstream cuts regions at a
    cos-sim value.

Cost: cos-sim is one matrix–vector product (O(n·d), \<1 s for n=10⁶,
d=50). The bottleneck is re-reading the three DESeq2 CSVs (8c
subset-overwrote the unfiltered objects). The merged region-level table
is built once and reused for both panels.

## Read embeddings, compute cos-sim to every label

```{r}
read_starspace_embeddings <- function(model_path, n_labels) {
  # StarSpace's model.tsv is one row per token, no header:
  #   <token>\t<v1>\t...\t<vd>
  # The trained label embeddings are written as the LAST n_labels rows, so
  # n_labels is the single knob that adapts every downstream step to a
  # 2-label model (Renin / Non_Renin) or a 3-label one
  # (Control / Tumoral / Renin).
  #
  # fread is ~10x faster than read.table on the 200 MB+ files this produces.
  if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
    embed <- data.table::fread(model_path, sep = "\t", header = FALSE,
                               showProgress = FALSE, data.table = FALSE)
  } else {
    embed <- read.table(model_path, sep = "\t", header = FALSE,
                        comment.char = "", quote = "",
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fill = TRUE)
  }
  embed <- embed[!is.na(embed[, 1]) & embed[, 1] != "", , drop = FALSE]

  n_row <- nrow(embed)
  if (n_labels < 2 || n_labels >= n_row) {
    stop(sprintf("n_labels = %s is not usable with %s rows in model.tsv.",
                 n_labels, format(n_row, big.mark = ",")))
  }
  label_idx   <- seq.int(n_row - n_labels + 1L, n_row)
  label_rows  <- embed[ label_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  region_rows <- embed[-label_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  # Positional split, verified by the "__label__" prefix: if the model was
  # trained with a different number of classes than n_labels claims, fail
  # here rather than silently treating a region vector as a label.
  if (!all(grepl("^__label__", label_rows[, 1]))) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "The last %d row(s) of model.tsv are not all '__label__' rows (got: %s). Set n_labels to the number of trained classes.",
      n_labels, paste(label_rows[, 1], collapse = ", ")))
  }
  if (any(grepl("^__label__", region_rows[, 1]))) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "model.tsv holds more than %d '__label__' rows; raise n_labels.", n_labels))
  }

  region_emb <- as.matrix(region_rows[, -1]); storage.mode(region_emb) <- "double"
  label_emb  <- as.matrix(label_rows[,  -1]); storage.mode(label_emb)  <- "double"

  list(
    region_names = region_rows[, 1],
    region_emb   = region_emb,
    label_emb    = label_emb,
    label_names  = gsub("^__label__", "", label_rows[, 1])
  )
}

# Row-wise L2 normalization — shared by every cosine computation below.
unit_rows <- function(M) {
  u <- M / pmax(sqrt(rowSums(M * M)), 1e-12)
  u[!is.finite(u)] <- 0
  u
}

emb <- read_starspace_embeddings(starspace_model_path, n_starspace_labels)

# Cosine sim of every region to every label — one BLAS call, n_regions x n_labels.
cos_mat <- unit_rows(emb$region_emb) %*% t(unit_rows(emb$label_emb))
colnames(cos_mat) <- emb$label_names
stopifnot(focus_label %in% colnames(cos_mat))

# Everything from here to 8j is written around a focal label and its
# complement:
#   cos_renin     = cos sim to focus_label
#   cos_non_renin = the region's BEST cos sim among all the other labels, i.e.
#                   "how strongly does this region belong to something that is
#                   not focus_label".
# With 2 labels cos_non_renin is exactly the old cos sim to __label__Non_Renin.
# With 3 it pools Control and Tumoral, which keeps the downstream top-N
# and GO steps a two-sided renin-vs-rest comparison. The per-label columns
# are carried alongside so a specific label can be inspected directly.
other_labels <- setdiff(colnames(cos_mat), focus_label)
cos_renin     <- as.numeric(cos_mat[, focus_label])
cos_non_renin <- if (length(other_labels) == 1) {
  as.numeric(cos_mat[, other_labels])
} else {
  do.call(pmax, as.data.frame(cos_mat[, other_labels, drop = FALSE]))
}

emb_df <- data.frame(
  region        = emb$region_names,
  cos_renin     = cos_renin,
  cos_non_renin = cos_non_renin,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
for (lb in colnames(cos_mat)) {
  emb_df[[paste0("cos_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", lb))]] <- as.numeric(cos_mat[, lb])
}
```

```{r}
# 8b loaded starspace_regions from bed/cluster_regions.csv; re-read it here
# so 8f can be run on its own without re-running 8b.

}

ss_dt <- data.frame(

  cluster = starspace_regions$title,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE

emb_df <- merge(emb_df, ss_dt, by = "region", all.x = TRUE)
```

## Re-read DESeq2 reports (unfiltered) and build the long-format table

```{r}
# Use data.table::fread if available (~5× faster on 100k+ rows); else read.csv.
read_deseq <- function(path) {
  df <- if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
    as.data.frame(data.table::fread(path))
  } else {
    read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  df$region <- paste(df$seqnames, df$start, df$end, sep = "_")
  df
}

dq_pn <- read_deseq(primary_normal_file); dq_pn$contrast <- "primary_normal"
dq_ph <- read_deseq(primary_high_file);   dq_ph$contrast <- "primary_high"
dq_an <- read_deseq(as_normal_file);      dq_an$contrast <- "as_normal"

# Per-contrast differential flag — same filter logic as 8c: raw pvalue for
# all three contrasts, matching filterRegions() in
# 3_plot_genomic_distributions.Rmd.
dq_pn$is_diff <- !is.na(dq_pn$pvalue) & dq_pn$pvalue < fdr &
                 abs(dq_pn$log2FoldChange) >= absFoldChange
dq_ph$is_diff <- !is.na(dq_ph$pvalue) & dq_ph$pvalue < fdr &
                 abs(dq_ph$log2FoldChange) >= absFoldChange
dq_an$is_diff <- !is.na(dq_an$pvalue) & dq_an$pvalue < fdr &
                 abs(dq_an$log2FoldChange) >= absFoldChange

keep_cols   <- c("region", "log2FoldChange", "contrast", "is_diff")
all_dq      <- rbind(dq_pn[, keep_cols], dq_ph[, keep_cols], dq_an[, keep_cols])
scatter_df  <- merge(all_dq, emb_df, by = "region")
scatter_df$contrast <- factor(scatter_df$contrast,
                              levels = c("primary_normal", "primary_high", "as_normal"))

# Per-contrast Spearman correlation, computed on ALL rows (not the
# plotting subsample). Annotated onto each facet below.
cor_df <- scatter_df %>%
  group_by(contrast) %>%
  summarise(rho = cor(log2FoldChange, cos_renin,
                      method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
            n   = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("rho = %.2f  (n = %s)",
                         rho, format(n, big.mark = ",")))
print(cor_df)
```

## (1) Scatter: cosine similarity to Renin label vs log2 fold change

```{r, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5}
plot_cos_vs_log2fc <- function(df, non_diff_cap = 20000, seed = 42) {
  has_ggrastr <- requireNamespace("ggrastr", quietly = TRUE)
  if (!has_ggrastr) {
    set.seed(seed)
    diff_df <- df[df$is_diff, ]
    nd_df   <- df[!df$is_diff, ]
    nd_df   <- nd_df[
      if (nrow(nd_df) > non_diff_cap) sort(sample.int(nrow(nd_df), non_diff_cap))
      else seq_len(nrow(nd_df)),
    ]
    df <- rbind(diff_df, nd_df)
    message(sprintf(
      "ggrastr not installed; plotting %s differential + %s non-differential points",
      format(nrow(diff_df), big.mark = ","),
      format(nrow(nd_df),   big.mark = ",")
    ))
  }

  # Status: Increase / Decrease / Non-differential. Levels ordered so grey
  # draws first, colored on top.
  df$status <- factor(
    ifelse(df$is_diff & df$log2FoldChange > 0, "Increase",
    ifelse(df$is_diff & df$log2FoldChange < 0, "Decrease", "Non-differential")),
    levels = c("Non-differential", "Decrease", "Increase")
  )
  df <- df[order(df$status), ]   # draw grey first, colored on top

  # Pivot to long: each region appears twice — once with cos_sim = cos_renin
  # (top row), once with cos_sim = cos_non_renin (bottom row). Keep only the
  # columns the plot needs to bound memory at ~half scatter_df's footprint.
  df_long <- bind_rows(
    df %>% transmute(contrast, log2FoldChange, status,
                     cos_sim = cos_renin,     label_target = "Renin"),
    df %>% transmute(contrast, log2FoldChange, status,
                     cos_sim = cos_non_renin, label_target = "Non-renin")
  ) %>%
    mutate(label_target = factor(label_target, levels = c("Renin", "Non-renin")))

  pt <- if (has_ggrastr) {
    ggrastr::rasterise(geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.3), dpi = 200)
  } else {
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.3)
  }

  ggplot(df_long, aes(log2FoldChange, cos_sim, colour = status)) +
    pt +
    facet_grid(label_target ~ contrast, switch = "y") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-absFoldChange, absFoldChange),
               colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_text(
      data = cor_df, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
      hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.3, size = 3.2, inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(Increase           = "#FF7F0E",   # tab:orange
                 Decrease           = "#1F77B4",   # tab:blue
                 `Non-differential` = "grey70"),
      breaks = c("Increase", "Decrease", "Non-differential"),
      name   = NULL
    ) +
    labs(x = "DESeq2 log2 fold change",
         y = "cosine similarity to label") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position  = "bottom",
          strip.placement  = "outside")
}

p_scatter <- plot_cos_vs_log2fc(scatter_df)

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "starspace_cos_vs_log2fc.svg"),
       p_scatter, width = 12, height = 9, units = "in", dpi = 200)

```

## (2) P(differential) vs cosine similarity — binned line plot

Replaces the cluster stacked bar. The nearest-label split is a hard cut
that throws away the continuous cos-sim information, which is precisely
what we want to inspect here. Binning regions by cos-sim quantile and
plotting the per-bin DE rate directly shows whether embedding distance
and DESeq2 calls co-vary — a rising curve means regions the embedding
places nearer the label are more often called differential.

This is a **descriptive** figure. Region sets are defined by the DESeq2
call and ranked by cosine (8g); nothing is cut at a cos-sim value, so
the curve can be read as evidence rather than as the thing that produced
the sets.

Bin edges come from quantiles of the full pooled cos-sim distribution,
so the same edges apply to every panel — the averaged and faceted views
are directly comparable.

```{r}
plot_pde_vs_cos <- function(df,
                            facet_by_contrast = TRUE,
                            n_bins = 20,
                            label_cols = NULL) {
  # ONE ROW PER LABEL (2026-09-06). `label_cols` is a named vector: the name
  # is the row strip, the value is that label's cosine column in `df`
  # (`cos_Renin`, `cos_Control`, `cos_Tumoral` -- written by the emb_df loop
  # in 8f). NULL keeps the historical single-row, Renin-only figure, so the
  # (2a) dual-axis caller and any older call site are unchanged.
  #
  # WHY EACH ROW GETS ITS OWN BIN EDGES. Edges are quantiles of that label's
  # OWN cosine distribution. Binning the Control row on Renin quantiles would
  # put most of its regions in one or two bins -- the three labels do not
  # share a cosine scale. The comparability the single-row version had
  # (same edges across contrast panels) is preserved WITHIN each row, which
  # is the comparison the figure is actually read for.
  if (is.null(label_cols)) label_cols <- c(Renin = "cos_renin")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(unname(label_cols), names(df))
  if (length(missing_cols))
    stop("plot_pde_vs_cos: column(s) not in df: ",
         paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))

  bin_one <- function(lab_name, cos_col) {
    x <- df[[cos_col]]
    brks <- quantile(x, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n_bins + 1),
                     na.rm = TRUE)
    d <- df
    d$cos_val <- x
    d$cos_bin <- cut(x, breaks = brks, include.lowest = TRUE)
    group_cols <- if (facet_by_contrast) c("contrast", "cos_bin") else "cos_bin"
    d %>%
      group_by(across(all_of(group_cols))) %>%
      summarise(
        n       = n(),
        cos_mid = median(cos_val),
        pct_inc = 100 * mean(is_diff & log2FoldChange > 0),
        pct_dec = 100 * mean(is_diff & log2FoldChange < 0),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(label = lab_name)
  }

  bin_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(label_cols, ~ bin_one(.y, .x)) %>%
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = names(label_cols))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(pct_inc, pct_dec),
                        names_to  = "direction",
                        values_to = "pct") %>%
    mutate(direction = recode(direction,
                              pct_inc = "Increase",
                              pct_dec = "Decrease"))

  multi <- length(label_cols) > 1
  p <- ggplot(bin_summary, aes(cos_mid, pct, colour = direction)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Increase = "#FF7F0E", Decrease = "#1F77B4"),
                        name = "DESeq2 direction") +
    labs(x = if (multi) "cosine similarity to the row's label (bin median)"
             else "cosine similarity to Renin label (bin median)",
         y = "% of regions called differential",
         caption = sprintf(
           "Quantile-binned within each row, %d bins, n_rows = %s%s",
           n_bins, format(nrow(df), big.mark = ","),
           if (facet_by_contrast) " (per-contrast)" else " (pooled across contrasts)"
         )) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  # free x: each label's cosine occupies a different range, so a shared axis
  # would compress two of the three rows into a sliver
  if (multi && facet_by_contrast) {
    p <- p + facet_grid(label ~ contrast, scales = "free_x")
  } else if (multi) {
    p <- p + facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_x")
  } else if (facet_by_contrast) {
    p <- p + facet_wrap(~ contrast)
  }
  p
}
```

### (2a) Pooled across contrasts — dual axis

Each direction gets its own cos-sim axis:

- **Increase (orange)** is binned by `cos_renin` and read against the
  **bottom** x-axis (cos sim to the Renin label).
- **Decrease (blue)** is binned by `cos_non_renin` and read against the
  **top** x-axis (cos sim to the Non-renin label).

Both axes share the same numerical scale (cos-sim is bounded in [-1, 1]
either way), they just measure distance to different label vectors. The
two binnings are independent — each line is in its own native axis
space.

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_pde_vs_cos_dual_axis <- function(df, n_bins = 20) {
  # ---- bin Increase by cos_renin ----
  brks_r <- quantile(df$cos_renin,
                     probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n_bins + 1),
                     na.rm = TRUE)
  bin_inc <- df %>%
    mutate(cos_bin = cut(cos_renin, breaks = brks_r, include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(cos_bin) %>%
    summarise(cos_mid = median(cos_renin),
              pct     = 100 * mean(is_diff & log2FoldChange > 0),
              n       = n(),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(direction = "Increase")

  # ---- bin Decrease by cos_non_renin ----
  brks_nr <- quantile(df$cos_non_renin,
                      probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n_bins + 1),
                      na.rm = TRUE)
  bin_dec <- df %>%
    mutate(cos_bin = cut(cos_non_renin, breaks = brks_nr, include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(cos_bin) %>%
    summarise(cos_mid = median(cos_non_renin),
              pct     = 100 * mean(is_diff & log2FoldChange < 0),
              n       = n(),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(direction = "Decrease")

  binned <- bind_rows(
    bin_inc %>% select(cos_mid, pct, n, direction),
    bin_dec %>% select(cos_mid, pct, n, direction)
  ) %>%
    mutate(direction = factor(direction, levels = c("Increase", "Decrease")))

  p <- ggplot(binned, aes(cos_mid, pct, colour = direction)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      name     = "cos sim to Renin label  (Increase line, bottom axis)",
      sec.axis = dup_axis(
        name = "cos sim to Non-renin label  (Decrease line, top axis)"
      )
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Increase = "#FF7F0E", Decrease = "#1F77B4"),
                        name = "DESeq2 direction") +
    labs(y = "% of regions called differential",
         caption = sprintf(
           "Quantile-binned (%d bins each). n_rows = %s (pooled across contrasts)",
           n_bins, format(nrow(df), big.mark = ",")
         )) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

}

p_pde_avg <- plot_pde_vs_cos_dual_axis(scatter_df, n_bins = 20)

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "starspace_pde_vs_cos_avg.svg"),
       p_pde_avg, width = 7, height = 4.5, units = "in")

```

### (2b) Faceted by contrast — primary_normal / primary_high / as_normal

```{r, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 4}
# One row per trained label, in `cluster_labels` order (focus first, so
# Renin / Control / Tumoral). Built from cluster_labels rather than hardcoded
# so a 2-label model still works -- it just draws two rows.
pde_label_cols <- setNames(
  paste0("cos_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", cluster_labels)),
  cluster_labels)

p_pde_facet <- plot_pde_vs_cos(scatter_df, facet_by_contrast = TRUE,
                               label_cols = pde_label_cols)

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "starspace_pde_vs_cos_by_contrast.svg"),
       p_pde_facet, width = 12,
       height = 3.4 * length(pde_label_cols), units = "in")
```

# 8g. Tornado signal profiles

## Reload intersection BEDs (for resumable execution)

```{r}
load_bed <- function(path) {
  readGeneric(path, chr = 1, start = 2, end = 3, strand = NULL,
              meta.cols = NULL, keep.all.metadata = FALSE, zero.based = FALSE,
              remove.unusual = FALSE, header = FALSE, skip = 0, sep = "\t")
}

# 8e writes one BED per (DESeq2 call x StarSpace label) plus the pooled
# "_nr" complement. 8g-8i use the PER-LABEL files, not the pool, so every
# feature set carries a single cluster identity and the two non-focal
# labels are kept APART: _r = Renin, _c = Control, _t = Tumoral.
#
# The grid is built from what is on disk rather than hand-listed, so a model
# with a different label vocabulary needs no edit here. Sets below
# `min_set_size` are dropped with a reason printed -- previously
# inc_control (30) and dec_r (3) were hardcoded out, which silently removed
# Control from the Increase row of every figure.
min_set_size <- 20

label_slug  <- function(x) gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)
# Suffix that 8e's bed_suffix() gave each label, inverted back to the label.
bed_labels  <- if (exists("cluster_labels")) {
  cluster_labels
} else {
  c(focus_label, "Control", "Tumoral")
}
suffix_of   <- function(lab) {
  if (identical(lab, focus_label)) "r" else tolower(label_slug(lab))
}
# Short alias used in variable and panel names: "r" for the focal label,
# first letter otherwise. Guard against two labels colliding on one letter.
short_of    <- function(lab) {
  if (identical(lab, focus_label)) "r" else substr(tolower(label_slug(lab)), 1, 1)
}
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(vapply(bed_labels, short_of, character(1))))

set_spec  <- list()
gr_list   <- list()
dropped   <- character(0)
for (cat in c("inc", "dec", "nd")) {
  for (lab in bed_labels) {
    bed <- file.path(bed_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.bed", cat, suffix_of(lab)))
    if (!file.exists(bed)) next
    gr <- load_bed(bed)
    nm <- paste(cat, short_of(lab), sep = "_")
    if (length(gr) < min_set_size) {
      dropped <- c(dropped, sprintf("%s (%d < %d)", nm, length(gr), min_set_size))
      next
    }
    assign(nm, gr)
    gr_list[[nm]]  <- gr
    set_spec[[nm]] <- list(
      label = lab,
      split = if (cat == "nd") "nd" else "diff")
  }
}
set_order <- names(set_spec)
stopifnot(length(set_order) > 0)
if (length(dropped))
  message("Feature sets below min_set_size, dropped: ",
          paste(dropped, collapse = ", "))

# Tag for cache + plot filenames. Caches and SVGs are keyed by filename
# alone, so the tag has to change whenever the SET MEMBERSHIP changes or a
# stale .rds comes back with the wrong feature groups. Folding the count in
# makes that automatic.
set_tag <- sprintf("perlabel%d", length(set_order))

# Everything downstream works off `gr_list`, not the individual variables.
gr_list <- gr_list[set_order]
message("Reloaded intersection BEDs:\n",
        paste(sprintf("  %-6s %9s regions  (%s)", set_order,
                      format(vapply(gr_list, length, integer(1)), big.mark = ","),
                      vapply(set_spec, `[[`, character(1), "label")),
              collapse = "\n"))
```

## Subset feature sets by top-N cos-sim ranking

Row count per subset is capped at a fixed top-N, and this is the **only**
selection applied to the tornado feature sets. Membership comes from the
DESeq2 call × StarSpace label intersection; ordering comes from the cosine
to that label. Each DESeq×StarSpace subset in `set_spec` stays, ranked by
the cosine similarity to **its own** StarSpace label:

- `inc_r`, `nd_r`          → keep top N by `cos_Renin`
- `dec_c`, `nd_c`          → keep top N by `cos_Control`
- `inc_t`, `dec_t`, `nd_t` → keep top N by `cos_Tumoral`

This is stricter than the old pooled rule: `cos_non_renin` was the *max*
over Control and Tumoral, so a Control set could be ranked by a region's
Tumoral affinity. Per-label ranking asks each set only about the cluster
it actually came from.

Why top-N: it gives **deterministic, balanced row counts per subset**
(every subset is at most `top_n`), so the heatmaps stop being dominated
by the huge `nd_*` blocks. The DESeq2 categorization is preserved. Note
`dec_c` (69) and `dec_t` (51) start well under `top_n`, so this step is a
no-op for them — they are bounded by their own size, not by N.

Needs `emb_df` from 8f, which writes one `cos_<label>` column per
StarSpace label alongside `cos_renin` / `cos_non_renin`.

```{r}
top_n <- 1000

# 8f slugs label names when it builds the per-label columns; match it.
cos_col <- function(label) paste0("cos_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", label))

needed_cols <- unique(vapply(set_spec, function(s) cos_col(s$label), character(1)))
if (!exists("emb_df") || !all(needed_cols %in% names(emb_df))) {
  stop("emb_df is missing column(s): ",
       paste(setdiff(needed_cols, if (exists("emb_df")) names(emb_df) else character(0)),
             collapse = ", "),
       ". Run 8f first — it writes one cos_<label> column per StarSpace label.")
}

# Key lookups: "chr_start_end" -> per-region cosine sim, one per label.
key_cos <- lapply(setNames(nm = needed_cols),
                  function(cn) setNames(emb_df[[cn]], emb_df$region))

gr_to_key <- function(gr) {
  paste(GenomicRanges::seqnames(gr),
        GenomicRanges::start(gr),
        GenomicRanges::end(gr), sep = "_")
}

# Filter a GRanges to its top-N regions by an arbitrary cos-sim lookup.
filter_top_by_cos <- function(gr, cos_lookup, top_n) {
  keys     <- gr_to_key(gr)
  cos_vals <- cos_lookup[keys]
  # Drop NAs (regions missing from emb_df). Then take top-N by cos.
  finite_ix <- which(is.finite(cos_vals))
  ord <- finite_ix[order(cos_vals[finite_ix], decreasing = TRUE)]
  gr[head(ord, top_n)]
}

sizes_before <- vapply(gr_list, length, integer(1))

# Every set ranked by the cosine to its own StarSpace label, and capped at
# top_n. This is the ONLY selection applied to the tornado feature sets:
# membership comes from the DESeq2 call x StarSpace label intersection, and
# ordering comes from the cosine. Nothing is matched, weighted, or
# thresholded on a third variable.
#
# baseMean matching was tried here and REMOVED (2026-09-05). It is not used
# in the differential section either, and measurement showed it does not do
# what it was meant to: baseMean correlates with bigWig coverage at only
# Spearman 0.41-0.68, and matching inc_r's baseMean exactly (2.70 -> 3.67)
# moved the PN bigWig gap just 4.44x -> 3.58x while pushing NR, NRT and TN
# FURTHER from parity. See notes/BASEMEAN_MATCHING_2026-09-04.md.
gr_list <- lapply(set_order, function(nm)
  filter_top_by_cos(gr_list[[nm]],
                    key_cos[[cos_col(set_spec[[nm]]$label)]], top_n))
names(gr_list) <- set_order

sizes_after <- vapply(gr_list, length, integer(1))

# top_n is a COUNT, so the cosine value it cuts at differs per set: for a
# 200,000-region set it is the top 0.5%, for dec_c (69) it is a no-op. Print
# the surviving cosine range so that truncation is visible, not implicit.
message(sprintf("Ranked by cosine, capped at top-%s:", format(top_n, big.mark = ",")))
for (nm in set_order) {
  cvs <- key_cos[[cos_col(set_spec[[nm]]$label)]][gr_to_key(gr_list[[nm]])]
  cvs <- cvs[is.finite(cvs)]
  message(sprintf(
    "  %-7s %9s -> %9s  (%5.1f%% kept; cos %.3f to %.3f, ranked by %s)",
    paste0(nm, ":"), format(sizes_before[[nm]], big.mark = ","),
    format(sizes_after[[nm]], big.mark = ","),
    100 * sizes_after[[nm]] / max(sizes_before[[nm]], 1),
    if (length(cvs)) min(cvs) else NA_real_,
    if (length(cvs)) max(cvs) else NA_real_,
    cos_col(set_spec[[nm]]$label)))
}
```

## Load bigWig signal files

Two bigwig configurations — one for each tornado plot we'll produce:

1.  **`bigwigs_avg`**: five group averages (Non-renin, WT, Recruited,
    Tumoral, Non-renin tumoral).
2.  **`bigwigs_samples`**: hand-picked individual replicate bigwigs.

`EnrichedHeatmap`'s `normalizeToMatrix` takes a GRanges of signal
coverage, which we import on the fly via `rtracklayer::import.bw()`.

PEPATAC output layout (renin + ENCODE pipelines):
`<base>/<sample_id>/aligned_mm10/<sample_id>_smooth.bw`

```{r}
# PEPATAC output roots. Renin and ENCODE samples live in sibling pipeline
# dirs under the same brickyard processed root.
renin_bw_base  <- "/project/shefflab/brickyard/results_pipeline/gomez_atac/results_pipeline_PEPATAC/renin_ATAC/results_pipeline"
encode_bw_base <- "/project/shefflab/brickyard/results_pipeline/gomez_atac/results_pipeline_PEPATAC/encode_ATAC/results_pipeline"
susztak_bw_base <- "/project/shefflab/brickyard/results_pipeline/gomez_atac/results_pipeline_PEPATAC/susztak_ATAC/results_pipeline"
ctrl_tumoral_bw_base <- "/project/shefflab/brickyard/results_pipeline/gomez_atac/results_pipeline_PEPATAC/ctrl_tumoral_ATAC/results_pipeline"

pepatac_bw <- function(sample_id, base = renin_bw_base) {
  file.path(base, sample_id, "aligned_mm10",
            paste0(sample_id, "_smooth.bw"))
}

# (1) Group-averaged bigwigs — one per sample group, for the high-level
# tornado. The PEPATAC `data/` sibling dir holds NR/WT/PH/PN/TN_average.bw.
# Order here = display order in legends and as columns in the heatmap.
avg_bw_dir <- "/project/shefflab/brickyard/results_pipeline/gomez_atac/results_pipeline_PEPATAC/data"

# Ordered renin -> non-renin, with the two tumoral tracks adjacent.
bigwigs_avg <- c(
  WT  = file.path(avg_bw_dir, "PN_average.bw"),   # wild-type renin cells (subset of Renin_Normal)
  PH  = file.path(avg_bw_dir, "PH_average.bw"),   # primary high (recruited)
  TN  = file.path(avg_bw_dir, "TN_average.bw"),   # tumoral (As4.1)
  NRT = file.path(avg_bw_dir, "NRT_average.bw"),  # non-renin tumoral (ctrl_tumoral_ATAC, 51 cell-line samples)
  NR  = file.path(avg_bw_dir, "NR_average.bw")    # non-renin (ENCODE controls)
)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(bigwigs_avg)))

# (2) Per-replicate bigwigs — for the per-sample tornado.
#
# Selected from metadata, not hand-listed, so the panel tracks the pipeline
# directories and the annotation sheet rather than drifting from them:
#
#   Renin_WT / Renin_Recruited / Renin_Tumoral : ALL samples
#   Control_Primary / Control_Tumoral          : KIDNEY tissue only
#
# Renin is a kidney gene, so non-kidney controls are the wrong comparison —
# and taking all of them would mean 178 ENCODE + 51 tumour-line columns.
#
# "Kidney" is decided two ways because the two control groups annotate
# tissue differently:
#   * Control_Primary carries the organ directly ("primary_kidney_cells").
#   * Control_Tumoral carries a CELL LINE in `Tissue` ("RENCA", "RAG"); which
#     lines are renal comes from the `tissue` column of
#     renin_annotation_sheet_add_tumoral_l4.csv ("RENCA_renal_carcinoma",
#     "RAG_renal_adenocarcinoma"). That sheet keys by abbreviated names
#     (RENCA_EVP_1) that do not match the pipeline directories, so the join
#     goes directory -> `Tissue` in renin_encode_atac.csv -> renal? in l4.
meta_bw <- read.csv(path.expand(
  "~/code/renin_atac/metadata/renin_encode_atac.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
l4_tissue <- read.csv(path.expand(
  "~/code/renin_atac/metadata/renin_annotation_sheet_add_tumoral_l4.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$tissue

kidney_re    <- "kidney|renal"
kidney_lines <- unique(sub("_.*$", "",
  l4_tissue[grepl(kidney_re, l4_tissue, ignore.case = TRUE)]))
is_kidney <- function(tis) {
  !is.na(tis) & (grepl(kidney_re, tis, ignore.case = TRUE) | tis %in% kidney_lines)
}

# sample id -> pipeline project, by scanning the PEPATAC roots.
#
# `exclude_projects` drops a whole PEPATAC project from the per-sample panel.
# susztak_ATAC is excluded: it is the only pre-pipestat run in the set
# (2021-2024, and the one whose assets.tsv pointed at a retired refgenie),
# so its tracks are the least comparable with the rest. Removing it leaves
# Control_Primary as 8 ENCODE kidney samples from a single processing batch.
exclude_projects <- "susztak_ATAC"

bw_roots <- c(renin_ATAC        = renin_bw_base,
              encode_ATAC       = encode_bw_base,
              susztak_ATAC      = susztak_bw_base,
              ctrl_tumoral_ATAC = ctrl_tumoral_bw_base)
bw_roots <- bw_roots[setdiff(names(bw_roots), exclude_projects)]
if (length(exclude_projects)) {
  message("Excluded PEPATAC project(s) from the per-sample panel: ",
          paste(exclude_projects, collapse = ", "))
}
sample_root <- unlist(lapply(bw_roots, function(r)
  stats::setNames(rep(r, length(list.files(r))), list.files(r))))
names(sample_root) <- sub("^[^.]*\\.", "", names(sample_root))   # drop the root prefix

take_all    <- c("Renin_WT", "Renin_Recruited", "Renin_Tumoral")
take_kidney <- c("Control_Primary", "Control_Tumoral")

sel <- meta_bw[meta_bw$Group_2 %in% c(take_all, take_kidney) &
               meta_bw$SampleID %in% names(sample_root), ]
sel <- sel[sel$Group_2 %in% take_all | is_kidney(sel$Tissue), ]

# Samples that have a pipeline directory but no Group_2 are reported, never
# silently dropped — As4.1_1 is one, and it is a real renin tumoral library.
renin_unassigned <- setdiff(list.files(renin_bw_base),
                            meta_bw$SampleID[nzchar(meta_bw$Group_2)])
if (length(renin_unassigned)) {
  message("NOTE: renin_ATAC sample(s) with no Group_2, EXCLUDED: ",
          paste(renin_unassigned, collapse = ", "))
}

# Long susztak ids are unreadable as a heatmap `name`; panels are titled by
# group anyway, so abbreviate purely for legends and messages. Inert while
# susztak_ATAC is in `exclude_projects`; kept so re-including it stays a
# one-word change.
short_name <- function(x) {
  x <- sub("^([0-9]+)-week_mouse_kidney_bulk_ATAC-seq_sample_", "\\1W_", x)
  sub("^P0_mouse_kidney_bulk_ATAC-seq_sample_", "P0_", x)
}
bigwigs_samples <- stats::setNames(
  pepatac_bw(sel$SampleID, sample_root[sel$SampleID]),
  short_name(sel$SampleID))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(names(bigwigs_samples)))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(bigwigs_samples)))

for (g in c(take_all, take_kidney)) {
  ids <- sel$SampleID[sel$Group_2 == g]
  message(sprintf("  %-16s n=%2d  (%s)", g, length(ids),
                  paste(sort(unique(sel$Tissue[sel$Group_2 == g])), collapse = ", ")))
}
excluded <- meta_bw[meta_bw$Group_2 %in% take_kidney &
                    meta_bw$SampleID %in% names(sample_root) &
                    !is_kidney(meta_bw$Tissue), ]
message(sprintf("  excluded %d non-kidney control sample(s) across %d tissue(s)",
                nrow(excluded), length(unique(excluded$Tissue))))

# 4T1_Adherent_2, 4T1_DAC_decitabine_3 and 4T1_MFP_2 never had chrM removed
# (2026-08-17 QC audit). All three are 4T1, so none survive the kidney
# filter — checked rather than assumed, since the filter could change.
chrm_dirty <- c("4T1_Adherent_2", "4T1_DAC_decitabine_3", "4T1_MFP_2")
if (any(chrm_dirty %in% sel$SampleID)) {
  message("NOTE: chrM not removed from ",
          paste(intersect(chrm_dirty, sel$SampleID), collapse = ", "),
          " (<=1.02x low; fine for display, not for FRiP/complexity).")
}
message(sprintf("Per-sample bigWigs: %d total", length(bigwigs_samples)))
```

## Sample -> group map for the per-sample tornado

The per-sample heatmap has 49 columns. Labelling each with its sample id is
unreadable and is not the comparison being made, so panels are ordered by
sample group and each group is named once, over the middle panel of its run.

Groups come from the `Group_2` column of `metadata/renin_encode_atac.csv`,
which already carries exactly these five levels — they are not re-derived
here. All 49 samples resolve; the chunk stops if any does not.

Two things this figure cannot hide, both from the 2026-08-17 QC audit
(`notes/data_quality_ENCODE_comparison_2026-08-17.md`):

* **`Control_Tumoral` is the 10 KIDNEY lines only** — RENCA (8) and RAG (2)
  — not all 51 in `ctrl_tumoral_ATAC`. Renin is a kidney gene, so the breast,
  lung, melanoma, colon and pancreatic lines are the wrong comparison, and 51
  columns would swamp the figure. Note this makes the per-sample
  `Control_Tumoral` a different set from `NRT_average.bw`, which pools all
  51 — the two figures are not showing the same samples for that group.
* **`WT_1` / `WT_2` are the same libraries as `Ren1c-YFP_1` / `Ren1c-YFP_2`**
  under two names. `Renin_WT` therefore shows four panels for two unique
  libraries. Set `drop_duplicate_wt <- TRUE` to plot the two unique ones.

```{r}
drop_duplicate_wt <- FALSE   # TRUE drops Ren1c-YFP_1/_2, the duplicate copies

# meta_bw was read when bigwigs_samples was built, just above.
meta_df <- meta_bw
stopifnot(all(c("SampleID", "Group_2") %in% names(meta_df)))

# bigwigs_samples is keyed by display name; recover the PEPATAC sample id
# from the path, which is the directory the bigwig sits in.
sample_id_of <- function(paths) basename(dirname(dirname(paths)))
sample_groups <- stats::setNames(
  meta_df$Group_2[match(sample_id_of(bigwigs_samples), meta_df$SampleID)],
  names(bigwigs_samples))

if (anyNA(sample_groups)) {
  stop("No Group_2 for: ",
       paste(names(sample_groups)[is.na(sample_groups)], collapse = ", "))
}

if (drop_duplicate_wt) {
  dup <- c("Ren1c-YFP_1", "Ren1c-YFP_2")
  bigwigs_samples <- bigwigs_samples[setdiff(names(bigwigs_samples), dup)]
  sample_groups   <- sample_groups[names(bigwigs_samples)]
  message("Dropped duplicate WT copies: ", paste(dup, collapse = ", "))
}

# Order panels by group so each group is one contiguous run — the column-title
# logic in build_tornado_heatmap_independent() depends on it.
group_levels    <- c("Renin_WT", "Renin_Recruited", "Renin_Tumoral",
                     "Control_Primary", "Control_Tumoral")
present         <- intersect(group_levels, unique(sample_groups))
ord             <- order(match(sample_groups, present))
bigwigs_samples <- bigwigs_samples[ord]
sample_groups   <- factor(sample_groups[ord], levels = present)
stopifnot(!is.unsorted(as.integer(sample_groups)))   # runs are contiguous

message("Per-sample panels, grouped:")
for (g in present) {
  nm <- names(sample_groups)[sample_groups == g]
  message(sprintf("  %-16s n=%2d  %s", g, length(nm), paste(nm, collapse = ", ")))
}
missing_groups <- setdiff(group_levels, present)
if (length(missing_groups)) {
  message("  NOT represented per-sample: ", paste(missing_groups, collapse = ", "),
          " (group-average figure only)")
}
```

## Per-track background scale factors

FRiP differs **17-fold** across these sample groups — 0.030 in sorted renin
primary vs 0.501 in the tumour lines
(`notes/data_quality_ENCODE_comparison_2026-08-17.md`). That is
signal-to-noise, not depth, so PEPATAC's per-sample normalisation does not
touch it and no rescaling can undo it. Measured over 20,000 matched
background bins the tracks agree to within 1.45x, but at the 99th percentile
they differ 4.7x — the whole disparity lives in the peaks.

Consequence for the figures: on one shared colour scale (cap = max q99 =
7.86e-08, set by Ctrl_tumoral) the two renin primary tracks reach only ~21%
of the ramp. They look washed out for reasons that have nothing to do with
chromatin.

`heatmap_norm = "background"` divides each track by its own genomic
background, so the colour becomes **fold enrichment over that track's noise
floor** and means the same thing in every column. Background is estimated
from random 10-kb genomic bins, NOT from peaks and NOT from the consensus
universe — peak-derived factors are biased exactly when composition differs,
which is the situation here. This is the standard signal-over-background
construction (MACS2 `fold_enrichment`, `bigwigCompare --ratio`).

That the result is not itself a FRiP artifact is checkable, and it checks
out: FRiP ranks WT lowest and Ctrl_tumoral highest, while `inc_r` enrichment
ranks them the other way round (7.31 vs 1.18), and `dec_c` flips completely
(0.89 in WT vs 6.54 in Ctrl_tumoral). A quality artifact would push the
high-FRiP tracks up everywhere.

Factors are cached — the bins are random but seeded, so the same factors
come back across runs.

```{r}
bg_bin_n     <- 20000
bg_bin_width <- 10000
bg_seed      <- 3

bw_background_factors <- function(bigwigs, n = bg_bin_n, w = bg_bin_width,
                                  seed = bg_seed, cache = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(cache) && file.exists(cache)) {
    f <- readRDS(cache)
    if (setequal(names(f), names(bigwigs))) {
      message("Background factors from cache: ", cache)
      return(f[names(bigwigs)])
    }
  }
  si <- GenomeInfoDb::seqinfo(rtracklayer::BigWigFile(bigwigs[[1]]))
  keep <- grep("^chr[0-9XY]+$", GenomeInfoDb::seqnames(si), value = TRUE)
  si <- si[keep]
  sl <- GenomeInfoDb::seqlengths(si)

  set.seed(seed)
  ch <- sample(names(sl), n, replace = TRUE, prob = sl / sum(sl))
  st <- as.integer(stats::runif(n, 1, sl[ch] - w))
  bg <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(ch, IRanges::IRanges(st, st + w - 1L))

  f <- vapply(bigwigs, function(path) {
    sig <- rtracklayer::import(path, which = bg, as = "RleList")
    v   <- rep(NA_real_, length(bg)); cc <- as.character(GenomicRanges::seqnames(bg))
    for (c1 in intersect(unique(cc), names(sig))) {
      i <- which(cc == c1)
      v[i] <- as.numeric(mean(IRanges::Views(sig[[c1]],
                GenomicRanges::start(bg)[i], GenomicRanges::end(bg)[i])))
    }
    mean(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))

  message(sprintf("Background factors (%s x %s-kb bins):", format(n, big.mark = ","), w/1000))
  for (nm in names(f)) message(sprintf("  %-14s %.4g", nm, f[[nm]]))
  message(sprintf("  spread across tracks: %.2fx", max(f)/min(f)))
  if (!is.null(cache)) saveRDS(f, cache)
  f
}

bg_avg     <- bw_background_factors(bigwigs_avg,
                 cache = file.path(plot_dir, "bg_factors_avg.rds"))
bg_samples <- bw_background_factors(bigwigs_samples,
                 cache = file.path(plot_dir, "bg_factors_samples.rds"))
```

## Define feature set + signal-binning helper

For each (feature, bigwig) pair, resize features to their midpoint, bin
the bigwig coverage into `w`-bp windows spanning ±`extend` around each
midpoint, then average across features per position. Output is a long-
format df with (`feature_set, sample_name, position, mean, sd, n`).

Defaults: **extend = 1000 bp, w = 20 bp** → 100 bins per row (50 per side).

```{r}
flatten_features_eh <- function(features, bigwigs, extend = 1000, w = 20,
                                verbose = TRUE) {
  ts  <- function() format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S")
  log <- function(...) if (verbose) message(sprintf("[%s] %s", ts(), paste0(...)))

  pos_vec <- c(
    seq(-extend + w / 2, -w / 2, by = w),
    seq( w / 2,  extend - w / 2, by = w)
  )
  out <- vector("list", length(features) * length(bigwigs))
  k <- 0L

  n_s <- length(bigwigs)
  n_f <- length(features)
  log(sprintf(">> flatten_features_eh: %d sample(s) × %d feature set(s) = %d calls; ",
              n_s, n_f, n_s * n_f),
      sprintf("extend=%d w=%d", extend, w))

  total_t0 <- Sys.time()
  for (si in seq_along(bigwigs)) {
    sample_name <- names(bigwigs)[si]
    bw_path     <- bigwigs[[sample_name]]

    log(sprintf("[%d/%d] importing %s ...", si, n_s, basename(bw_path)))
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    signal <- rtracklayer::import(bw_path)
    log(sprintf("    imported in %.1fs; %s ranges, %.0f MB in memory",
                as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs"),
                format(length(signal), big.mark = ","),
                object.size(signal) / 1e6))

    for (fi in seq_along(features)) {
      feature_set <- names(features)[fi]
      feat_gr     <- features[[feature_set]]
      if (length(feat_gr) == 0) {
        log(sprintf("    [%d/%d] %s × %s: skipped (0 features)",
                    fi, n_f, sample_name, feature_set))
        next
      }
      log(sprintf("    [%d/%d] %s × %s: %s features, normalizeToMatrix ...",
                  fi, n_f, sample_name, feature_set,
                  format(length(feat_gr), big.mark = ",")))
      t1 <- Sys.time()
      mid <- GenomicRanges::resize(feat_gr, width = 1, fix = "center")
      mat <- EnrichedHeatmap::normalizeToMatrix(
        signal, target = mid,
        value_column = "score",
        extend = extend, mean_mode = "w0", w = w
      )
      log(sprintf("        done in %.1fs; mat dim %d × %d",
                  as.numeric(Sys.time() - t1, units = "secs"),
                  nrow(mat), ncol(mat)))

      k <- k + 1L
      out[[k]] <- data.frame(
        feature_set = feature_set,
        sample_name = sample_name,
        position    = pos_vec,
        mean        = colMeans(mat, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd          = matrixStats::colSds(as.matrix(mat), na.rm = TRUE),
        n           = nrow(mat),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
    rm(signal); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  }
  log(sprintf(">> total wall time: %.1f min",
              as.numeric(Sys.time() - total_t0, units = "mins")))
  do.call(rbind, out[seq_len(k)])
}

# DESeq2 × StarSpace intersection feature sets for tornado + heatmap — one
# per (DESeq2 call × StarSpace label), as declared in `set_spec` in 8g.
# The two non-focal labels are kept SEPARATE throughout (_c = Control,
# _t = Tumoral); the pooled "_nr" union is 8j's, not this section's. With a
# 3-label model the grid is inc/dec/nd × Renin/Control/Tumoral, minus any
# set under `min_set_size`.
# Each was ranked top-N by its own label's cosine. The pooled "_nr" sets are
# no longer used here.
feats <- do.call(GRangesList, gr_list)
```

# 8h. Tornado line plots

±1000 bp around each region's midpoint, w = 20 bp bins (100 bins total).
Lines are per-bin mean across regions; **ribbons show mean ± SEM**
(standard error of the per-region values at that bin). Color palette is
shared with the heatmap top-annotation lines in 8i.

## Helpers

```{r}
# Shared discrete color palette for the feature groups. Same colors in
# tornado_facets() lines and build_tornado_heatmap_independent()
# top-annotation curves so the two figures cross-reference visually.
#
# The seven hues below are the historical assignment and are kept so old
# figures stay comparable — inc_r red, nd_r blue/cyan, as in the original
# 4-set palette. `set_spec` is now built from whatever labels the model has
# (§8g), so any set without an entry here — inc_c, dec_r, or a set from a
# different label vocabulary — gets a hue appended from hue_pal(). Never
# reorder the fixed block: the colors are referenced in written-up figures.
feature_group_colors <- c(
  inc_r = "#F8766D",   # red    — Increase × Renin
  inc_t = "#C49A00",   # gold   — Increase × Tumoral
  dec_c = "#53B400",   # green  — Decrease × Control
  dec_t = "#00C094",   # teal   — Decrease × Tumoral
  nd_r  = "#00B6EB",   # blue   — Non-diff × Renin
  nd_c  = "#A58AFF",   # purple — Non-diff × Control
  nd_t  = "#FB61D7"    # pink   — Non-diff × Tumoral
)

missing_cols <- setdiff(set_order, names(feature_group_colors))
if (length(missing_cols)) {
  extra <- scales::hue_pal(h = c(15, 375), l = 45)(length(missing_cols))
  names(extra) <- missing_cols
  feature_group_colors <- c(feature_group_colors, extra)
  message("Palette extended for ", length(missing_cols), " new set(s): ",
          paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
}

# Line + ribbon plot, faceted by sample. `ribbon` controls the band:
#   "sem"  = mean ± SEM (default — narrow at high n; shows mean reliability)
#   "sd"   = mean ± SD (wider — shows region-to-region spread)
#   "ci95" = mean ± 1.96 × SEM
#   "none" = line only
tornado_facets <- function(df, title,
                           y_label      = "mean signal",
                           ribbon       = c("sem", "sd", "ci95", "none"),
                           ribbon_alpha = 0.2,
                           hline_zero   = FALSE,
                           group_colors = feature_group_colors) {
  ribbon <- match.arg(ribbon)

  if (ribbon != "none") {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        .half = dplyr::case_when(
          ribbon == "sem"  ~ sd / sqrt(pmax(n, 1)),
          ribbon == "ci95" ~ 1.96 * sd / sqrt(pmax(n, 1)),
          ribbon == "sd"   ~ sd,
          TRUE             ~ 0
        ),
        .ymin = mean - .half,
        .ymax = mean + .half
      )
  }

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(position))
  if (ribbon != "none") {
    p <- p +
      geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .ymin, ymax = .ymax, fill = feature_set),
                  alpha = ribbon_alpha, colour = NA) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors, guide = "none")
  }
  p <- p +
    geom_line(aes(y = mean, colour = feature_set), linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors) +
    facet_wrap(~ sample_name) +
    labs(x = "position relative to region midpoint",
         y = y_label, colour = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right")
  if (hline_zero) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
                        linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey50")
  }
  p
}
```

## (2) Per-sample tornado

To keep memory bounded for the 33-sample run, subsample each feature set
to at most 5,000 regions before normalizeToMatrix. The mean signal curve
is essentially indistinguishable from the full set, since each bin still
averages over thousands of regions.

```{r}
subsample_feats <- function(gr_list, max_n = 5000, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  GRangesList(lapply(gr_list, function(g) {
    if (length(g) <= max_n) g
    else g[sort(sample.int(length(g), max_n))]
  }))
}
subsample_n <- 5000   # set to NULL to disable

feats_for_samples <- if (is.null(subsample_n)) {
  feats
} else {
  subsample_feats(feats, max_n = subsample_n)
}
vapply(feats_for_samples, length, integer(1))

                            sprintf("df_samples_1k_w20_%s.rds", set_tag))

  readRDS(df_samples_rds)
} else {

  out <- flatten_features_eh(feats_for_samples, bigwigs_samples,
                              extend = 1000, w = 20)
  saveRDS(out, df_samples_rds)
  out
}
```

# 8i. Per-region tornado heatmaps

±1000 bp / w = 20 bp matrices, same feature sets as 8h. Each row is a
region; columns are bin positions. Color = signal (raw) or fraction of
total per-(sample, bin) (sum-to-one normalization).

## Helpers

```{r}
compute_tornado_matrices <- function(features, bigwigs, extend = 1000, w = 20,
                                     verbose = TRUE) {
  ts  <- function() format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S")
  log <- function(...) if (verbose) message(sprintf("[%s] %s", ts(), paste0(...)))

  group_names <- names(features)
  combined <- do.call(c, lapply(group_names, function(fn) {
    g <- features[[fn]]
    if (length(g) == 0) return(g)
    mcols(g) <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(.group = rep(fn, length(g)))
    g
  }))
  group_factor <- factor(combined$.group, levels = group_names)
  target_mid   <- GenomicRanges::resize(combined, width = 1, fix = "center")
  log(sprintf(">> compute_tornado_matrices: %d sample(s) × %d feature group(s) → ",
              length(bigwigs), length(features)),
      sprintf("%s total regions, %d bins", format(length(target_mid), big.mark = ","),
              2 * extend / w))

  mats <- vector("list", length(bigwigs))
  names(mats) <- names(bigwigs)
  for (i in seq_along(bigwigs)) {
    sn <- names(bigwigs)[i]
    log(sprintf("  [%d/%d] %s: import + normalizeToMatrix ...",
                i, length(bigwigs), sn))
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    sig <- rtracklayer::import(bigwigs[[i]])
    mats[[sn]] <- EnrichedHeatmap::normalizeToMatrix(
      sig, target_mid,
      value_column = "score",
      extend = extend, mean_mode = "w0", w = w
    )
    log(sprintf("      done in %.1fs",
                as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))
    rm(sig); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  }

  list(
    mats         = mats,
    group_factor = group_factor,
    extend       = extend,
    w            = w
  )
}

# Apply (or skip) sum_to_one across feature_sets, then compute one shared
# color function spanning every (sample, group, bin) cell. Lets multiple
# build_tornado_heatmap_independent() calls (e.g. diff vs nd splits)
# share an exact color scale.
# Divide every sample matrix by that track's own genomic background, turning
# the plotted value into fold enrichment. Errors rather than silently passing
# raw signal through if a factor is missing — a half-normalised panel set is
# worse than an un-normalised one.
apply_bg_norm <- function(mats, bg_factors) {
  if (is.null(bg_factors)) {
    stop("normalize = \"background\" needs bg_factors; ",
         "run the 'Per-track background scale factors' chunk in 8g.")
  }
  missing <- setdiff(names(mats), names(bg_factors))
  if (length(missing)) {
    stop("No background factor for: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  }
  for (sn in names(mats)) mats[[sn]] <- mats[[sn]] / bg_factors[[sn]]
  mats
}

compute_unified_col_fun <- function(tornado_data,
                                    normalize = c("none", "sum_to_one", "background"),
                                    col_pal = c("white", "darkblue"),
                                    cap_quantile = 0.99,
                                    bg_factors = NULL) {
  normalize    <- match.arg(normalize)
  mats         <- tornado_data$mats
  group_factor <- tornado_data$group_factor

  if (normalize == "background") mats <- apply_bg_norm(mats, bg_factors)

  if (normalize == "sum_to_one") {
    for (sn in names(mats)) {
      mat <- mats[[sn]]
      group_bin_means <- vapply(levels(group_factor), function(g) {
        colMeans(mat[group_factor == g, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
      }, numeric(ncol(mat)))
      bin_totals <- rowSums(group_bin_means, na.rm = TRUE)
      mats[[sn]] <- sweep(mat, 2, pmax(bin_totals, 1e-12), "/")
    }
  }

  cap <- max(vapply(mats,
                    function(m) stats::quantile(m, cap_quantile, na.rm = TRUE),
                    numeric(1)))
  message(sprintf("compute_unified_col_fun: %d sample(s), %d group(s), cap = %.4f",
                  length(mats), length(levels(group_factor)), cap))
  circlize::colorRamp2(c(0, cap), col_pal)
}

# Per-sample INDEPENDENT row sorting: each sample's heatmap is built
# standalone with its own per-group row order, sorted by that sample's
# enriched_score. Returns a NAMED LIST of EnrichedHeatmap objects.
# Render the list with draw_independent_heatmaps() below.
build_tornado_heatmap_independent <- function(tornado_data,
                                              display_groups = NULL,
                                              normalize = c("none", "sum_to_one", "background"),
                                              col_pal = c("white", "darkblue"),
                                              cap_quantile = 0.99,
                                              col_fun = NULL,
                                              use_raster = TRUE,
                                              group_colors = feature_group_colors,
                                              bg_factors = NULL,
                                              sample_groups = NULL,
                                              verbose = TRUE) {
  normalize    <- match.arg(normalize)
  mats         <- tornado_data$mats
  group_factor <- tornado_data$group_factor

  if (normalize == "background") mats <- apply_bg_norm(mats, bg_factors)

  if (normalize == "sum_to_one") {
    for (sn in names(mats)) {
      mat <- mats[[sn]]
      group_bin_means <- vapply(levels(group_factor), function(g) {
        colMeans(mat[group_factor == g, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
      }, numeric(ncol(mat)))
      bin_totals <- rowSums(group_bin_means, na.rm = TRUE)
      mats[[sn]] <- sweep(mat, 2, pmax(bin_totals, 1e-12), "/")
    }
  }

  if (!is.null(display_groups)) {
    keep_rows <- group_factor %in% display_groups
    mats <- lapply(mats, function(m) m[keep_rows, , drop = FALSE])
    group_factor <- factor(group_factor[keep_rows], levels = display_groups)
  }

  if (is.null(col_fun)) {
    cap <- max(vapply(mats,
                      function(m) stats::quantile(m, cap_quantile, na.rm = TRUE),
                      numeric(1)))
    col_fun <- circlize::colorRamp2(c(0, cap), col_pal)
  } else {
    cap <- environment(col_fun)$breaks[length(environment(col_fun)$breaks)]
  }
  legend_title <- switch(normalize,
    sum_to_one = "fraction",
    background = "fold over\nbackground",
    "signal")

  line_cols <- group_colors[levels(group_factor)]
  if (any(is.na(line_cols))) {
    fallback <- scales::hue_pal()(length(levels(group_factor)))
    line_cols[is.na(line_cols)] <- fallback[is.na(line_cols)]
  }

  if (verbose) {
    message(sprintf("  independent sort: %d sample heatmap(s), %d feature groups, color cap = %.4f",
                    length(mats), length(levels(group_factor)), cap))
  }

  heatmaps <- lapply(seq_along(mats), function(i) {
    sn  <- names(mats)[i]
    mat <- mats[[sn]]

    new_order <- unlist(lapply(levels(group_factor), function(g) {
      gi <- which(group_factor == g)
      gi[order(EnrichedHeatmap::enriched_score(mat[gi, , drop = FALSE]),
               decreasing = TRUE)]
    }), use.names = FALSE)
    mat_sorted <- mat[new_order, , drop = FALSE]
    gf_sorted  <- group_factor[new_order]

    # Row-block titles only on the leftmost panel — keeps right panels compact.
    row_title <- if (i == 1L)
                   levels(group_factor)
                 else
                   rep("", length(levels(group_factor)))

    # Column title. With `sample_groups` the 33 per-sample panels are labelled
    # by SAMPLE GROUP rather than by sample id: the name is drawn once, over
    # the middle panel of each run of same-group samples, and blank elsewhere.
    # `mats` must already be ordered by group for the runs to be contiguous —
    # asserted where sample_groups is built.
    col_title <- if (is.null(sample_groups)) {
      sn
    } else {
      g   <- sample_groups[[sn]]
      idx <- which(sample_groups[names(mats)] == g)
      if (i == idx[ceiling(length(idx) / 2)]) g else ""
    }

    EnrichedHeatmap::EnrichedHeatmap(
      mat_sorted,
      col          = col_fun,
      name         = sn,
      column_title = col_title,
      row_split    = gf_sorted,
      row_title    = row_title,
      cluster_rows = FALSE,
      use_raster   = use_raster,
      show_heatmap_legend  = (i == 1L),
      heatmap_legend_param = list(title = legend_title),
      top_annotation = ComplexHeatmap::HeatmapAnnotation(
        enriched = EnrichedHeatmap::anno_enriched(
          gp = grid::gpar(col = line_cols, lty = 1, lwd = 1.2)
        )
      )
    )
  })
  names(heatmaps) <- names(mats)
  heatmaps
}

# Render a list of standalone heatmaps side-by-side in one SVG. Each
# heatmap is drawn in its own grid viewport, so per-sample row orders
# are preserved (no shared alignment from the `+` operator).
draw_independent_heatmaps <- function(heatmaps,
                                       svg_path,
                                       column_title = NULL,
                                       panel_width_in = 2.5,
                                       height_in = 10) {
  n <- length(heatmaps)
  total_width <- n * panel_width_in + 1.5   # reserve space for legend

  svg(svg_path, width = total_width, height = height_in)
  grid::grid.newpage()

  if (!is.null(column_title)) {
    grid::grid.text(column_title, x = 0.5, y = 0.97,
                    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold"))
    grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(y = 0.48, height = 0.92))
  }

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(
    layout = grid::grid.layout(nrow = 1, ncol = n)
  ))

  for (i in seq_along(heatmaps)) {
    grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.col = i))
    ComplexHeatmap::draw(
      heatmaps[[i]],
      newpage = FALSE,
      show_heatmap_legend = (i == 1L),
      show_annotation_legend = (i == 1L)
    )
    grid::popViewport()
  }
  grid::popViewport()
  if (!is.null(column_title)) grid::popViewport()
  dev.off()
}
```

```{r}
# Normalization: "sum_to_one" or "none"
heatmap_norm <- "background"   # "none" | "sum_to_one" | "background"

td_avg_rds <- file.path(plot_dir, sprintf("td_avg_1k_w20_%s.rds", set_tag))
# The cache is keyed only by filename, so a cache written before a track was
# added to bigwigs_avg — or before a feature set was added to set_spec —
# would silently come back short a column or a row block. Recompute unless
# it holds exactly the tracks AND the feature groups we asked for, in order.
cached_td_avg <- if (file.exists(td_avg_rds)) readRDS(td_avg_rds) else NULL
if (!is.null(cached_td_avg) &&
    !identical(names(cached_td_avg$mats), names(bigwigs_avg))) {
  message("Cached td_avg has tracks [", paste(names(cached_td_avg$mats), collapse = ", "),
          "] but bigwigs_avg is [", paste(names(bigwigs_avg), collapse = ", "),
          "] - recomputing.")
  cached_td_avg <- NULL
}
if (!is.null(cached_td_avg) &&
    !identical(levels(cached_td_avg$group_factor), set_order)) {
  message("Cached td_avg has groups [",
          paste(levels(cached_td_avg$group_factor), collapse = ", "),
          "] but set_order is [", paste(set_order, collapse = ", "),
          "] - recomputing.")
  cached_td_avg <- NULL
}
td_avg <- if (!is.null(cached_td_avg)) {
  message("Loading cached td_avg from ", td_avg_rds)
  cached_td_avg
} else {
  message("Computing td_avg (", length(bigwigs_avg),
          " bigwig imports + normalizeToMatrix)...")
  out <- compute_tornado_matrices(feats, bigwigs_avg, extend = 1000, w = 20)
  saveRDS(out, td_avg_rds)
  out
}

# Unified color scale across BOTH splits (diff and nd) of the avg heatmap.
avg_col_fun <- compute_unified_col_fun(td_avg, normalize = heatmap_norm,
                                       bg_factors = bg_avg)

# Panel membership comes from set_spec$split, so dropping an empty set in
# 8g removes it from the right split automatically.
splits_of <- function(which_split)
  set_order[vapply(set_spec, `[[`, character(1), "split") == which_split]
diff_groups <- splits_of("diff")   # inc_*, dec_* for every surviving label
nd_groups   <- splits_of("nd")     # nd_*  for every surviving label

# Row blocks per split are no longer fixed (Control is now its own set in the
# Increase row), so the canvas has to grow with them or the blocks compress.
# 2.5 in/block reproduces the historical 10 in at 4 blocks exactly, so old
# figures are unchanged and only the larger grids get taller.
split_height_in <- function(groups) max(10, 2.5 * length(groups))

# Split 1: differential — one row block per (call x label) that cleared
# min_set_size, so with a 3-label model this is up to 6, not the old 4.
draw_independent_heatmaps(
  build_tornado_heatmap_independent(
    td_avg, display_groups = diff_groups,
    normalize = heatmap_norm, col_fun = avg_col_fun, bg_factors = bg_avg
  ),
  svg_path = file.path(plot_dir,
                       sprintf("tornado_heatmap_averages_diff_%s_1k_w20_%s.svg",
                                heatmap_norm, set_tag)),
  column_title = sprintf("Differential (%s) — group averages [%s]",
                          paste(diff_groups, collapse = ", "), heatmap_norm),
  panel_width_in = 2.5,
  height_in      = split_height_in(diff_groups)
)

# Split 2: non-differential — one row block per surviving label
draw_independent_heatmaps(
  build_tornado_heatmap_independent(
    td_avg, display_groups = nd_groups,
    normalize = heatmap_norm, col_fun = avg_col_fun, bg_factors = bg_avg
  ),
  svg_path = file.path(plot_dir,
                       sprintf("tornado_heatmap_averages_nd_%s_1k_w20_%s.svg",
                                heatmap_norm, set_tag)),
  column_title = sprintf("Non-differential (%s) — group averages [%s]",
                          paste(nd_groups, collapse = ", "), heatmap_norm),
  panel_width_in = 2.5,
  height_in      = split_height_in(nd_groups)
)
```
