# 8k. Cosine quartiles within a fixed DESeq2 category

Every other figure in this document either selects on cosine (8g-8i) or
lets the DESeq2 call vary with it (8f), so none of them can separate
"the embedding recovers what DESeq2 already found" from "the embedding
adds something DESeq2 missed".

This one holds the DESeq2 category **fixed** and varies cosine inside it.
Take all `inc` regions, split them into quartiles by cosine to the Renin
label, and measure the renin-minus-non-renin signal in each. If Q4 > Q1
the embedding is ordering regions the fold-change call did not, and that
statement is immune to the circularity objection because every region
plotted carries the same DESeq2 label.

Two deliberate departures from 8g:

* **No intersection with a StarSpace label.** `inc_r` is already a
  cosine-based selection; using it would put cosine on both sides again.
  The input here is the raw `inc` / `dec` key set from 8c.
* **No top-N.** Quartiles are defined on the full category, so the cosine
  range is not truncated.

Signal comes from the same five group-average bigWigs as 8h, so the two
figures are directly comparable. Note this is bigWig coverage, not the
quantity DESeq2 modelled — for a number to quote in the text, recompute
the delta from the normalised count matrix that fed `dds`
(`1_featureCounts_quantilesNormalization.R`); the bigWigs are depth-
normalised per sample and then averaged, which is a different
normalisation.

```{r}
q_extend  <- 1000
q_w       <- 20
q_center  <- 200     # bp each side of the midpoint used for the scalar delta
q_renin     <- c("WT", "PH", "TN")     # renin-expressing group averages
q_non_renin <- c("NRT", "NR")          # non-renin group averages
stopifnot(all(c(q_renin, q_non_renin) %in% names(bigwigs_avg)))

# inc / dec as plain key vectors from 8c, turned back into GRanges.
keys_to_gr <- function(keys) {
  # Anchored at the END: 33 chromosomes in this universe contain underscores
  # (chr1_GL456210_random and friends, 270 regions), so splitting on "_" gives
  # a ragged list that do.call(rbind, .) silently recycles into wrong
  # coordinates. Same regex as write_set_bed() in 8e.
  m  <- stringr::str_match(keys, "^(.+)_([0-9]+)_([0-9]+)$")
  ok <- !is.na(m[, 1])
  if (any(!ok)) {
    warning(sum(!ok), " key(s) did not parse as <chrom>_<start>_<end>; dropped.")
  }
  GenomicRanges::GRanges(
    seqnames = m[ok, 2],
    ranges   = IRanges::IRanges(as.integer(m[ok, 3]), as.integer(m[ok, 4])))
}

cos_renin_col <- cos_col(focus_label)
cos_r_lookup  <- key_cos[[cos_renin_col]]

# One feature set per (category, quartile).
build_quartiles <- function(keys, tag, n_q = 4) {
  cv   <- cos_r_lookup[keys]
  keep <- is.finite(cv)
  keys <- keys[keep]; cv <- cv[keep]
  if (!length(keys)) return(list())
  qs <- stats::quantile(cv, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n_q + 1), na.rm = TRUE)
  qs[1] <- -Inf; qs[length(qs)] <- Inf
  bin <- cut(cv, unique(qs), include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
  out <- lapply(seq_len(n_q), function(q) keys_to_gr(keys[which(bin == q)]))
  names(out) <- sprintf("%s_Q%d", tag, seq_len(n_q))
  out[lengths(out) > 0]
}

q_feats <- c(build_quartiles(inc, "inc"), build_quartiles(dec, "dec"))
message("Cosine-quartile feature sets (ranked by ", cos_renin_col, "):\n",
        paste(sprintf("  %-8s %7s regions", names(q_feats),
                      format(lengths(q_feats), big.mark = ",")),
              collapse = "\n"))

q_rds <- file.path(plot_dir, "df_cos_quartiles_1k_w20.rds")
if (file.exists(q_rds)) {
  df_q <- readRDS(q_rds)
  message("Loaded cached quartile profiles: ", q_rds)
} else {
  df_q <- flatten_features_eh(q_feats, bigwigs_avg,
                              extend = q_extend, w = q_w)
  saveRDS(df_q, q_rds)
}

df_q$category <- sub("_Q[0-9]+$", "", df_q$feature_set)
df_q$quartile <- as.integer(sub("^.*_Q", "", df_q$feature_set))
```

## (1) Profiles by quartile

```{r, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 6}
p_q_prof <- ggplot(df_q,
                   aes(position, mean,
                       colour = factor(quartile),
                       group  = interaction(quartile, sample_name))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(category ~ sample_name) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = sprintf("%s quartile\n(Q4 = closest)", focus_label),
                         option = "C", end = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "distance from region midpoint (bp)",
       y = "mean bigWig coverage",
       title = sprintf("Signal by %s cosine quartile, DESeq2 category held fixed",
                       focus_label)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "starspace_cos_quartile_profiles.svg"),
       p_q_prof, width = 11, height = 6)

```

## (2) Renin minus non-renin delta per quartile

The scalar is the mean over the central +/-`q_center` bp. Averaging
positions and then regions is the same number as averaging regions and
then positions, so this is exact for the mean; the ribbon is a
across-region SEM propagated from the per-position `sd` and `n` that
`flatten_features_eh` returns, and it ignores the correlation between
adjacent bins, so read it as indicative rather than as a test.

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
q_core <- subset(df_q, abs(position) <= q_center)

q_grp <- q_core %>%
  mutate(arm = ifelse(sample_name %in% q_renin, "renin", "non_renin")) %>%
  group_by(category, quartile, arm) %>%
  summarise(sig = mean(mean),
            sem = sqrt(sum((sd / sqrt(n))^2)) / n(),
            .groups = "drop")

q_delta <- q_grp %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(sig, sem)) %>%
  mutate(delta = sig_renin - sig_non_renin,
         delta_sem = sqrt(sem_renin^2 + sem_non_renin^2))

p_q_delta <- ggplot(q_delta, aes(factor(quartile), delta,
                                 group = category, colour = category)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = delta - delta_sem, ymax = delta + delta_sem),
                width = 0.15) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = sprintf("%s cosine quartile (Q4 = closest to label)", focus_label),
       y = sprintf("mean coverage, renin (%s) - non-renin (%s)",
                   paste(q_renin, collapse = "/"),
                   paste(q_non_renin, collapse = "/")),
       title = "Does embedding distance order regions within a fixed DESeq2 call?") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "starspace_cos_quartile_delta.svg"),
       p_q_delta, width = 7, height = 4)


knitr::kable(q_delta, digits = 4)
```

# 8j. GO enrichment weighted-rank plot — refined Renin vs Non-renin regions

Same GREAT enrichment + renin-term weighted-rank procedure as
`4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd` sections 4d/4e, but applied to the refined
region classification that combines both DESeq2 and StarSpace evidence:

- **Renin** = `inc_r` — regions that (1) showed increased accessibility
  in renin samples in the DESeq2 analysis AND (2) fell in the StarSpace
  Renin cluster from 8b.
- **Non-renin** = everything else in the StarSpace cluster universe,
  i.e. `inc_nr ∪ dec_r ∪ dec_nr ∪ nd_r ∪ nd_nr`. These are regions that
  failed at least one of the two criteria above.

Background: genome-wide null (no explicit `bg` arg to GREAT). Using the
cluster union as background here would push foreground ≈ background for
the Non-renin set (it covers ~99% of the universe), collapsing every
hypergeometric p-value toward 1 and emptying the post-filter table. The
genome-wide null lets both sets produce real enrichment tables that the
weighted-rank step can score against each other.

## Load packages

```{r}
library(rGREAT)
```

## Build refined Renin / Non-renin GRanges from 8e intersection BEDs

Reload from disk so this chunk is independent of the in-memory `gr_list`
/ `inc_r` / etc., which 8g has already narrowed by top-N and by the
cosine ranking. 8j is still a two-sided Renin-vs-rest comparison and so
keeps using the pooled `_nr` BEDs that 8e writes alongside the per-label
ones; `inc_nr ∪ dec_nr ∪ nd_nr` is exactly the Control ∪ Tumoral union
that 8g now handles as separate sets.

```{r}
load_bed_8j <- function(path) {
  readGeneric(path, chr = 1, start = 2, end = 3, strand = NULL,
              meta.cols = NULL, keep.all.metadata = FALSE,
              zero.based = FALSE, remove.unusual = FALSE,
              header = FALSE, skip = 0, sep = "\t")
}

inc_r_full  <- load_bed_8j(file.path(bed_dir, "inc_r.bed"))
inc_nr_full <- load_bed_8j(file.path(bed_dir, "inc_nr.bed"))
dec_r_full  <- load_bed_8j(file.path(bed_dir, "dec_r.bed"))
dec_nr_full <- load_bed_8j(file.path(bed_dir, "dec_nr.bed"))
nd_r_full   <- load_bed_8j(file.path(bed_dir, "nd_r.bed"))
nd_nr_full  <- load_bed_8j(file.path(bed_dir, "nd_nr.bed"))

renin_refined_gr <- inc_r_full
non_renin_gr     <- c(inc_nr_full, dec_r_full, dec_nr_full,
                      nd_r_full,  nd_nr_full)

message(sprintf(
  "Refined sets: Renin = %s regions (inc_r), Non-renin = %s regions (everything else)",
  format(length(renin_refined_gr), big.mark = ","),
  format(length(non_renin_gr),     big.mark = ",")
))

ss_query <- GenomicRanges::GRangesList(
  Renin     = renin_refined_gr,
  Non_renin = non_renin_gr
)
```

## Run GREAT GO Biological Process enrichment

```{r}
ss_getBioEnrichment <- function(gr) {
  # No explicit background: when the Non-renin set covers ~99% of the
  # cluster universe, foreground ≈ background and every hypergeometric
  # p-value collapses toward 1, leaving the filter step with zero rows.
  # Testing each set against the genome-wide null lets both produce real
  # enrichment tables that the weighted-rank step can compare.
  job <- rGREAT::submitGreatJob(gr, species = "mm10")
  tb  <- rGREAT::getEnrichmentTables(job)
  tb$`GO Biological Process`
}

ss_enrichment <- lapply(names(ss_query), function(s) {
  ss_getBioEnrichment(ss_query[[s]])
})
names(ss_enrichment) <- names(ss_query)
```

## Weighted rank of renin-related GO terms

```{r}
# Shared with 4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd. 8j used to carry its own `ss_*` copies
# that had drifted back to the pre-fix versions of all four functions -- see
# the header of go_enrichment_functions.R for what each of them got wrong.
source("go_enrichment_functions.R")
```

```{r}
# Same order of operations as 4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd 4d/4e, which matters:
#
#   go_results_all  FULL tables + a `sig` flag  -> what getRank/getRankWeight see
#   go_results      significance-filtered       -> ONLY used to choose terms
#
# 8j used to rank and weight the FILTERED tables. A term clearing the filter in
# one region set but not the other then contributed 0 for the other set,
# term_sum collapsed to one value, and rank_weight came out exactly 1.0 — a
# spurious 100% bar that looked identical to a genuinely exclusive term.
ss_all <- lapply(ss_enrichment, function(df) {
  df$sig <- !is.na(df$Hyper_Adjp_BH) &
            df$Hyper_Adjp_BH <= 0.1 &
            df$Hyper_Foreground_Gene_Hits >= 3
  df
})

# filterEnrichment() keys on Hyper_Foreground_Gene_Hits, the column
# 4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd has actually run against. Fail with the real column
# list rather than a bare object-not-found if the GREAT server ever renames it.
need <- c("Hyper_Adjp_BH", "Hyper_Foreground_Gene_Hits", "Hyper_Fold_Enrichment",
          "name", "ID")
absent <- setdiff(need, names(ss_enrichment[[1]]))
if (length(absent)) {
  stop("GREAT table is missing: ", paste(absent, collapse = ", "),
       "\n  Columns present: ", paste(names(ss_enrichment[[1]]), collapse = ", "),
       "\n  (older rGREAT called the hits column Hyper_Observed_Gene_Hits)")
}

ss_go <- lapply(ss_all, filterEnrichment)

# Guard: empty enrichment table after filtering usually means foreground ≈
# background (collapsing hypergeometric p-values toward 1). Print sizes so
# this is easy to diagnose if it happens.
n_rows_per_set <- sapply(ss_go, nrow)
message("Filtered enrichment table sizes: ",
        paste(sprintf("%s = %d", names(n_rows_per_set), n_rows_per_set),
              collapse = ", "))
if (any(n_rows_per_set == 0)) {
  stop("Empty enrichment table(s): ",
       paste(names(n_rows_per_set)[n_rows_per_set == 0], collapse = ", "),
       ". Check the foreground vs background sizes in ss_getBioEnrichment().")
}

# Terms from the FILTERED tables (significant in at least one set), by GO graph
# ancestry — not the old keyword regex.
ss_renin_terms <- getReninGOTerms(ss_go)
message(sprintf("Renin-related GO terms (GO-ancestry): %d", length(ss_renin_terms)))

# Rank and weight on the FULL tables.
ss_rank_dfs <- lapply(names(ss_all), function(s) getRank(ss_all[[s]], group = s))
names(ss_rank_dfs) <- names(ss_all)
ss_rank_dfs <- getRankWeight(ss_rank_dfs, ss_renin_terms)

ss_plot_df <- do.call(rbind, ss_rank_dfs)
ss_plot_df <- ss_plot_df[!is.na(ss_plot_df$name), ]
rownames(ss_plot_df) <- NULL

# getRank() is fold-only by design — the two region sets differ greatly in
# size, so their hypergeometric p-values are not comparable across groups.
# The old rank_pvalue / rank_pvalue_weight columns no longer exist.
ss_plot_df <- ss_plot_df %>%
  select(name, Group, sig,
         Rank_weight = rank_weight,
         Rank_fold   = rank_fold,
         Fold        = Hyper_Fold_Enrichment)

ss_plot_df$Group <- factor(ss_plot_df$Group, levels = c("Renin", "Non_renin"))

ss_term_order <- ss_plot_df %>%
  filter(Group == "Renin") %>%
  arrange(desc(Rank_weight)) %>%
  mutate(labels = factor(name)) %>%
  head(50)

ss_plot_df <- filter(ss_plot_df, name %in% ss_term_order$name)
ss_new_order <- ss_plot_df %>%
  filter(Group == "Renin") %>%
  arrange(desc(Rank_weight)) %>%
  mutate(labels = factor(name))
```

# 8l. Top GO terms per StarSpace cluster

One panel per StarSpace label cluster — `Renin`, `Control`, `Tumoral` —
showing that cluster's top enriched GO Biological Process terms.

This is a deliberately simpler question than 8j. 8j scores *renin-related*
terms on the **refined** Renin set (`inc_r`, i.e. DESeq2 ∩ StarSpace) against
everything else. 8l drops the DESeq2 axis entirely and asks what each cluster
of the embedding is enriched for on its own terms, using the cluster
membership from 8b (`ss_sets`) with no DESeq2 intersection.

`go_top_n` selects between two foregrounds, and the chunk is written to
produce either from the same code:

* **`NULL` — the whole cluster.** Every region assigned to that label, all
  68,503 / 212,698 / 141,287 of them. This is the honest description of what
  the embedding partitioned the universe into.
* **an integer — the N regions closest to that cluster's own label** by cosine
  similarity to the label embedding (`cos_mat`, computed in 8f). Cluster
  assignment is already nearest-label, so this keeps the same ranking and just
  cuts it off at N: the cluster's core rather than its whole basin. A cluster
  of 212,698 regions is half the universe and its enrichment is diluted by
  everything sitting near the decision boundary; the top N is the sharper
  question, at the cost of no longer describing the full cluster.

The two are written to different files and neither overwrites the other, so
they can be read side by side.

**Background is the cluster universe** (all three clusters pooled = the
consensus peak universe the model was trained on), not the genome-wide null
8j is forced to use. The three clusters partition that universe, so no cluster
is anywhere near 100% of it — `Renin` is 16%, `Tumoral` 33%, `Control` 50% —
and the collapse-toward-p=1 problem that made 8j use the genome-wide null does
not arise here. Using the universe matters: against a genome-wide null every
ATAC peak set enriches for "sits near a gene", and all three panels would
return near-identical developmental terms. Against the universe those cancel
and what is left is what separates one cluster from the other two.

**GREAT runs locally**, via `rGREAT::great()`, and not by choice: the online
server `4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd` submits to with `submitGreatJob()` **no
longer exists**. `great.stanford.edu` returns NXDOMAIN from public DNS
(checked against 8.8.8.8 from a compute node, 2026-09-06), while
`stanford.edu` and `bioconductor.org` resolve normally from the same node —
so this is the hostname being gone, not a cluster firewall. 4c/4d in
`4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd` cannot be re-run as written; its existing outputs
predate the shutdown.

Local mode applies the same `basalPlusExt` regulatory-domain rule (5 kb
upstream / 1 kb downstream, extended to 1 Mb) against
`TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene` TSSs, so the enrichment model is GREAT's,
but the column names differ from the web server's (`fold_enrichment_hyper` /
`p_adjust_hyper` here vs `Hyper_Fold_Enrichment` / `Hyper_Adjp_BH` there) and
the GO annotation comes from the locally installed `org.Mm.eg.db` rather than
whatever vintage the server held. Numbers are therefore close to, but not
byte-identical with, what 4c produced.

Ranking follows `4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd` 4c (`plotTopEnrichedGO`): keep terms
with fold enrichment ≥ `go_fold_min` (2, as in 4c) and ≥ 3 foreground gene
hits, then take the smallest BH-adjusted p-values.

**That filter empties the table for the whole-cluster foreground, and the
reason is structural.** `fold_enrichment_hyper` is
`observed_gene_hits / (gene_set_size * n_gene_gr / n_gene_total)`. A
foreground covering a large fraction of the background touches nearly every
gene, so `observed_gene_hits` saturates at `gene_set_size` and the ratio is
pinned near 1 no matter how real the biology is. Measured on the whole-cluster
run (job 19384856): the **maximum** fold over ~9,280 terms was 1.24 for Renin
(16% of the universe), 1.05 for Control (50%) and 1.08 for Tumoral (33%) — and
for Control and Tumoral that maximum equals the third quartile, which is the
saturation signature. Nothing anywhere near 2 exists to be kept.

So this is not a threshold to lower; a "fold enrichment" axis spanning
1.00–1.05 measures the foreground's size, not its biology. It is the reason
`go_top_n` exists: at 5,000 regions each cluster is ~1.2% of the universe and
the gene hits stop saturating. The p-values remain informative in both cases
(2,018 / 986 / 489 terms at BH ≤ 0.05 on the whole clusters), which is why the
failure shows up only in the fold channel. The hypergeometric (gene-based) columns are used, which
are the `Hyper_*` columns 4c and 8j rank on; local `great()` calls them
`fold_enrichment_hyper` / `p_adjust_hyper` and reports the binomial
region-based test alongside them in the same table.

## Cluster region sets and background

```{r}
# ss_sets comes from 8b and is keyed by the trained label; keys_to_gr() is the
# underscore-safe key parser defined in 8k (33 chromosomes in this universe
# have underscores in their names, so a plain strsplit gives wrong coordinates).
cluster_go_labels <- intersect(cluster_labels, names(ss_sets))

# NULL = whole cluster; an integer = that cluster's N regions closest to its
# own label. The batch runners in src/cluster_go_run/ pass this through the
# GO_TOP_N environment variable, so both variants come from this one chunk
# rather than from a forked copy of it.
go_top_n <- if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("GO_TOP_N"))) {
  as.integer(Sys.getenv("GO_TOP_N"))
} else {
  NULL
}
go_tag <- if (is.null(go_top_n)) "" else sprintf("_top%d", go_top_n)

# cos_mat (8f) is regions x labels. It carries label colnames but NO rownames
# -- 8f keeps the region names beside it in emb$region_names and joins by
# column -- so index it through an explicit name -> row lookup rather than by
# character subscript, which silently fails with "subscript out of bounds".
cos_row_of <- if (is.null(go_top_n)) NULL else {
  stats::setNames(seq_along(emb$region_names), emb$region_names)
}

# Rank each cluster's members by cosine to THAT cluster's label, not to
# focus_label, so every panel is cut the same way relative to its own centre.
take_cluster_core <- function(keys, label, n) {
  if (is.null(n)) return(keys)
  stopifnot(label %in% colnames(cos_mat))
  ri <- cos_row_of[keys]
  if (anyNA(ri)) {
    stop(sum(is.na(ri)), " region(s) of cluster ", label,
         " are absent from model.tsv; cos_mat and ss_sets disagree.")
  }
  cv <- cos_mat[ri, label]
  keys[order(cv, decreasing = TRUE)][seq_len(min(n, length(keys)))]
}

cluster_go_keys <- lapply(cluster_go_labels, function(lab)
  take_cluster_core(ss_sets[[lab]], lab, go_top_n))
names(cluster_go_keys) <- cluster_go_labels
cluster_go_gr <- lapply(cluster_go_keys, keys_to_gr)

# Union of all clusters = the consensus universe. Built from ss_sets, NOT from
# cluster_go_keys: the background is the whole universe in both variants, so a
# top-N foreground is tested against everything rather than against a
# correspondingly shrunken background, and the two figures stay comparable.
cluster_go_bg <- keys_to_gr(unlist(ss_sets[cluster_go_labels], use.names = FALSE))

message(sprintf("8l foregrounds (%s): %s | background: %s regions",
                if (is.null(go_top_n)) "whole cluster"
                  else sprintf("top %d closest to own label", go_top_n),
                paste(sprintf("%s=%s", names(cluster_go_gr),
                              format(lengths(cluster_go_gr), big.mark = ",")),
                      collapse = ", "),
                format(length(cluster_go_bg), big.mark = ",")))

# Same GO_enrichment/ directory the 4_greatGOenrichment.Rmd figures live in.
go_plot_dir <- file.path(plot_dir, "GO_enrichment")
dir.create(go_plot_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Run local GREAT, one table per cluster

```{r}
# exclude = NULL, not the "gap" default: resolving the default fetches the mm10
# gap track from UCSC.
#
# Cost is NOT driven by the foreground size, which is the intuitive guess and
# is wrong. Measured on this data with 8 cores: three whole clusters
# (68,503 + 212,698 + 141,287 regions) took 23m47s, three top-5,000
# foregrounds took 13m18s. A 40x smaller foreground bought 1.8x, because the
# per-cluster fixed cost -- extending the TSS set, overlapping the
# 422,488-region background, and scoring 14,957 gene sets -- is paid whatever
# the foreground size. Shrinking go_top_n further is a sharper QUESTION, not a
# faster run.
#
# Cached, so the figure can be re-cut without re-running any of that. Delete
# the RDS to force a refresh after re-clustering.
cluster_go_rds <- file.path(go_plot_dir,
                            sprintf("cluster_go_bp_tables%s.rds", go_tag))

# Parallel over gene sets. Under SLURM take the allocation; interactively stay
# single-core rather than forking 40 workers on a shared login node.
great_cores <- max(1L, as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "1")))

if (file.exists(cluster_go_rds)) {
  cluster_go_tabs <- readRDS(cluster_go_rds)
  message("Loaded cached GREAT tables: ", cluster_go_rds)
} else {
  cluster_go_tabs <- lapply(names(cluster_go_gr), function(lab) {
    message("GREAT (local) for cluster ", lab, " ...")
    res <- rGREAT::great(cluster_go_gr[[lab]],
                         gene_sets   = "GO:BP",
                         tss_source  = "TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene",
                         background  = cluster_go_bg,
                         exclude     = NULL,
                         min_gene_set_size = 5,
                         cores       = great_cores)
    rGREAT::getEnrichmentTable(res)
  })
  names(cluster_go_tabs) <- names(cluster_go_gr)
  saveRDS(cluster_go_tabs, cluster_go_rds)
}

stopifnot(all(c("description", "fold_enrichment_hyper", "p_adjust_hyper",
                "observed_gene_hits") %in% names(cluster_go_tabs[[1]])))
```

## Plot: p-value bars + fold-enrichment line, one panel per cluster

```{r, fig.width = 3.74, fig.height = 1.77}
go_n_terms    <- 5    # terms per panel; 3 x 5 bars is what fits in 95 mm
go_fold_min   <- if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("GO_FOLD_MIN"))) {
  as.numeric(Sys.getenv("GO_FOLD_MIN"))    # 4c's threshold; see the prose on
} else {                                   # why relaxing it is usually wrong
  2
}
go_name_chars <- 20   # x labels are vertical, so this is a HEIGHT budget

# The vertical x labels are the binding constraint on a 45 mm figure, and the
# numbers here are measured off rendered output, not estimated: at 6 pt one
# character is ~1.2 mm tall, so 20 characters cost ~22 mm of the 45 and leave
# the panel ~13 mm. 22 characters already squeezes the panel to ~10 mm, which
# is not enough for a dual axis.
#
# Wrapping the labels onto two shorter lines was tried and is worse. It buys
# back ~7 mm of height, but two 6 pt lines are ~4.2 mm wide against a ~5 mm bar
# pitch, so neighbouring labels very nearly touch and it stops being obvious
# which line belongs to which bar. One truncated line per bar reads cleanly.
#
# Truncation is lossy for GO BP names, so the full untruncated names are in the
# table printed under this chunk -- read the figure with that table.

# 4c's filter, on the local-GREAT column names.
pick_top_go <- function(tb, lab, n = go_n_terms) {
  keep <- subset(tb, is.finite(p_adjust_hyper) &
                     fold_enrichment_hyper >= go_fold_min &
                     observed_gene_hits >= 3)
  if (!nrow(keep)) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "No GO term passes the 4c filter for cluster %s (fold >= %g, >= 3 gene hits). %s",
      lab, go_fold_min,
      sprintf("Max fold over %s terms was %.3f.",
              format(nrow(tb), big.mark = ","),
              max(tb$fold_enrichment_hyper, na.rm = TRUE))))
    return(NULL)
  }
  keep <- head(keep[order(keep$p_adjust_hyper), , drop = FALSE], n)
  # Foregrounds of 68k-213k regions drive adjusted p-values below double
  # precision, and p == 0 would make -log10() infinite and blow up the y
  # scale. Floor at the smallest representable double (-log10 = 307.65) and
  # say so, rather than plotting Inf or silently dropping the strongest term.
  floored <- keep$p_adjust_hyper < .Machine$double.xmin
  if (any(floored)) {
    message(sprintf("  %s: %d term(s) at p_adjust_hyper = 0, floored to %.3g",
                    lab, sum(floored), .Machine$double.xmin))
  }
  data.frame(cluster = lab,
             term    = keep$description,
             negLogP = -log10(pmax(keep$p_adjust_hyper, .Machine$double.xmin)),
             fold    = keep$fold_enrichment_hyper,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

go_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(cluster_go_tabs), function(lab)
  pick_top_go(cluster_go_tabs[[lab]], lab)))

# Fail here, with the numbers, rather than let an empty frame reach order()
# and surface as "order(integer(0), NULL, ...)" 40 minutes into a batch job.
if (is.null(go_df) || !nrow(go_df)) {
  stop("No GO term passes the filter in ANY cluster. Max fold_enrichment_hyper: ",
       paste(sprintf("%s = %.3f", names(cluster_go_tabs),
                     vapply(cluster_go_tabs,
                            function(d) max(d$fold_enrichment_hyper, na.rm = TRUE),
                            numeric(1))), collapse = ", "),
       " against go_fold_min = ", go_fold_min,
       ".\n  A whole-cluster foreground saturates the gene hits and pins the ",
       "fold near 1 -- set go_top_n (GO_TOP_N) rather than lowering the ",
       "threshold. See the prose above this chunk.")
}

go_df$cluster <- factor(go_df$cluster, levels = names(cluster_go_tabs))
go_df <- go_df[order(go_df$cluster, go_df$negLogP, decreasing = c(FALSE, TRUE),
                     method = "radix"), ]

# One x level per ROW, not per term: a term enriched in two clusters would
# otherwise share a level and be drawn in both panels by facet_wrap.
go_df$x <- factor(seq_len(nrow(go_df)))
go_labels <- ifelse(nchar(go_df$term) > go_name_chars,
                    paste0(substr(go_df$term, 1, go_name_chars - 1), "\u2026"),
                    go_df$term)
names(go_labels) <- go_df$x

# ggplot has ONE y scale, so the secondary axis needs a single global factor.
# That is the better choice anyway: it keeps fold enrichment comparable across
# the three panels instead of rescaling each one independently.
go_scale <- max(go_df$negLogP) / max(go_df$fold)

p_cluster_go <- ggplot(go_df, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = negLogP), fill = "grey75", colour = NA, width = 0.75) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fold * go_scale, group = 1),
            colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_point(aes(y = fold * go_scale), shape = 21, colour = "black",
             fill = "white", size = 0.8, stroke = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ cluster, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = go_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name     = expression(-log[10] * "(FDR)"),
    expand   = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)),
    # Two lines, not one: a 15-character axis title at 8 pt is ~23 mm tall
    # against a ~13 mm panel, so "fold enrichment" on one line has its top
    # clipped off by the device edge. Splitting it spends horizontal space,
    # which this figure has.
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / go_scale, name = "fold\nenrichment")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1,
                                    size = 6, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.x     = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y     = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.ticks       = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, colour = "black"),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.6, "mm"),
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black",
                                    margin = margin(0.3, 0.8, 0.3, 0.8, "mm")),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black",
                                    linewidth = 0.25),
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    panel.border     = element_rect(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
    panel.spacing    = unit(1.5, "mm"),
    plot.margin      = margin(1, 1, 1, 1, "mm"),
    legend.position  = "none")

# Named apart from 4c's top_enriched_go_*.svg, which are the DESeq2 sets.
cluster_go_svg <- file.path(
  go_plot_dir, sprintf("top_enriched_go_starspace_clusters%s.svg", go_tag))
ggsave(cluster_go_svg, p_cluster_go, width = 95, height = 45, units = "mm")
message("Saved: ", cluster_go_svg)

knitr::kable(go_df[, c("cluster", "term", "negLogP", "fold")], digits = 3)

p_cluster_go
```
